confirmed.title: /api/auth/me is not started early, and the community gate (plus the settings and access reads on every page) waits for it
confirmed.routes: /community (its whole body); the shell reads on every route
confirmed.cause: AuthContext.tsx:53-67 sends /api/auth/me from a mount effect, after the entry has downloaded and React has mounted; bootFetch.ts:195-212 does not prime it. useCommunityAccess builds its key as `isLoaded ? user?.id ?? 'guest' : ''` (access.tsx:107) and asks nothing until auth is loaded, and CommunityGate draws the page from that answer. WalletContext also waits for authLoaded before /api/settings/public (WalletContext.tsx:173-175). /community is not a rewritten document either (worker/index.ts:878), so it also waits on resolve.
confirmed.measured:
CDP trace, /community on a phone: resolve 2182→2424 → /api/auth/me 2446→2766 → /api/community/access 2868→3196 → the h1 (LCP) at 3360. Audit LCP 3192 and 3476 ms.

On the product page, access and settings leave only at 3973 ms, after me (2827→3729).
confirmed.fix:
Prime /api/auth/me in bootRequests. On /community, also prime /api/community/access and use that anonymous answer when me reports a guest. Inline the apex resolve answer in the /community document (see the category finding).

Expected: −0.4 to −0.6 s on /community; the shell reads leave about 0.5 s earlier elsewhere.
reasons:
The /community part of the finding holds up in both the code and a fresh live measurement. The "shell reads on every route" part is overstated.

Code, re-read at 7c7190b:
- AuthContext.tsx:53-67 sends /api/auth/me from the AuthProvider mount effect.
- bootRequests (bootFetch.ts:195-212) primes only resolve, /api/home, /api/products and /api/products/:slug. It never primes /me.
- useCommunityAccess sets `key = isLoaded ? user?.id ?? 'guest' : ''` (access.tsx:107) and asks nothing while key is ''. CommunityGate (access.tsx:230-232) draws `fallback ?? null`, which is blank, until access arrives.
- The gate only mounts after `resolved` (App.tsx AppContent `if (!resolved) return <RouteFallback/>`). So /api/community/access leaves at max(me, resolve) plus a mount.
- /community is not in run_worker_first, and worker/index.ts:878 rewrites only / and /products. The document is the plain static shell: no inline resolve, no fetch preload.
- Nothing else handles this: no srcset, edge rule or lazy wrapper changes the chain.

Server cost is not the cause. With curl, a guest's /me takes about 50-60 ms server-side (TTFB minus TLS). The phone's 210-460 ms for /me is Slow-4G latency plus bandwidth shared with the chunks that load at mount.

Live re-measurement on the phone profile (360x800, DPR 3, CPU x4, 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps, cold), 4 interleaved rounds per variant. The fix was emulated with an init-script fetch hook. It fires at the exact moment bootFetch runs, which it detects through bootFetch's own `getElementById('lv-resolve')` call, and it hands the early response to the app's later fetch.
- Baseline: me leaves about 200 ms after boot, and access waits for it. LCP median 2980 ms, h1 2929.
- B, /me primed at boot only: LCP 2650 (−330 ms).
- C, /me and /api/community/access primed together: LCP 2448 (−530 ms). In 3 of 4 runs the card is the first paint (FCP = LCP).
- D, C plus an instant resolve (stands in for the inline answer): LCP 2396 (−584 ms). The inline resolve adds only about 50 ms at the median. It only matters on a slow-resolve outlier like live run 2, where resolve took 1054 ms.
- So the claimed −0.4 to −0.6 s on /community is confirmed.

What is mis-rated:
1. "Elsewhere" is close to zero. For a guest, nothing visible waits on me, access or settings:
   - BottomNav and ServicesGrid keep the community tab and tile while the answer is unknown.
   - IQD prices do not wait for settings (CurrencyContext settingsLoaded matters only for USD display).
   - Product.tsx uses settings only for the delivery note and the gini link (lines 880-924).
   - Measured on /product/esun-pla-plus, baseline vs /me primed, in the paired round where boot time matched: LCP 4100 vs 4036 ms (−64, noise). In that round LCP came before settings returned, so the product LCP does not wait on settings. The finding's "access and settings leave at 3973" on the product page is true but costs no display time.
2. Reach is limited. The cost applies to the CommunityGate routes (/community, /community/*, /u/:username, /requests, /requests/:id, /followed-stores). While the community is shut it is just the maintenance card, and the nav tab and services tile are hidden, so few visitors land there. When the community opens, the chain gets longer: the lazy Community chunk and its data only start after me → access.
3. The /me prime is worth more than the finding says for signed-in users. ProtectedRoute and AdminRoute (/cart, /checkout, /orders, /profile, admin, merchant) show RouteFallback until /me returns, and a signed-in /me does a D1 JOIN.

Fix nuance: the primed access request carries the same cookie as /me, so its answer is valid for whichever user /me reports, not only for a guest. Adopt it for `me.user?.id ?? 'guest'` unless clearPrimedRequests has bumped the session epoch. Limiting it to guests leaves members on the slow path for no reason. Inlining resolve for /community needs it added to run_worker_first, which costs a Worker call per document, for about 50 ms at the median. That part is low priority.

Evidence (scratch only): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-authme/ab.mjs and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-authme/ab.log

The finding is real on /community, but it is rated too broadly. Only the gated routes pay for it. The "shell reads on every route" part does not delay what is drawn.

Code (perf/live 7c7190b):
- AuthContext.tsx:53-67 sends /api/auth/me from a mount effect.
- bootRequests in bootFetch.ts:195-212 primes resolve, home, products and product, but never me.
- useCommunityAccess builds its key as `isLoaded ? user?.id ?? 'guest' : ''` (access.tsx:107) and asks nothing while the key is '' (access.tsx:118-121).
- CommunityGate returns null until access arrives (access.tsx:229, `if (!access) return <>{fallback ?? null}</>`). /community has no fallback (App.tsx:949), so the whole body is blank.
- `<Community/>` is a lazy chunk (App.tsx:316) inside the gate, so on an open community the chain is longer still: me, then access, then the Community chunk, then its data.
- /community is not rewritten (worker/index.ts:874 mainOpening covers only / and /products).
- The finding did not mention ProtectedRoute and AdminRoute (App.tsx:506-520). Behind 36 routes (cart, checkout, orders, profile) they return RouteFallback until isLoaded, so the page's lazy chunk does not even start before me answers. This applies to signed-in users. I could not measure it, since I did not sign in.

Live, my own A/B (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-authme-b/ab2.mjs, results in ab2.log):

Where the finding is mis-rated:
1. "Shell reads on every route" has no measured display cost. The bottom bar keeps the community tab until access answers (BottomNav.tsx:171-177). Prices fall back to dinars or the cached rate before settings arrive (CurrencyContext.tsx). On / (A/B, 4 rounds) the LCP h1 does not depend on me: median 2716 vs 2612, within noise pair by pair. access and settings did not even leave earlier on / (B 2876-3149 ms vs A 2997-3288 ms) because their components mount later. 3. The fix's "use the anonymous access answer when me reports a guest" is narrower than needed. A primed access request carries the cookie, so its answer belongs to whoever the session is. It can serve any viewer once me confirms the same session.
4. Business weight today is limited. The community is closed live, and the bottom bar hides the tab once access answers. So cold /community loads come mostly from direct links, admins and allow-listed testers. Every one of those loads pays the full cost, and so will every visitor once the community opens.

The maintenance-card h1 goes 2929 → 2346 ms. The same gain applies to every CommunityGate route. Product page: about 0 (paired round LCP 4100 vs 4036 ms). Other routes: nothing visible waits on these reads for a guest, so 0. Signed-in ProtectedRoute pages (cart, orders, checkout) should gain about 0.2-0.3 s from the /me prime alone; not measured, because measuring it needs a login.

Measured on the live site with a phone profile (Slow-4G, CPU ×4, cold, emulated priming at the moment bootFetch runs). confirmed.title: Live search: every keystroke runs 5 dependent D1 round trips and returns full cards
confirmed.routes: the search panel on /, /products?search=, and every TopBarSearch
confirmed.cause: LiveSearch.tsx:166-170 sends /api/products?search=<prefix>&limit=6 after its debounce. Each new prefix is a new cache key, so it always misses. searchProducts (store.ts:416 onward) runs loadSynonyms (store.ts:373-380, re-read on every request; there is no per-isolate memo, unlike the pricing inputs), then the vocabulary range scan, then the postings, then the products read together with pricing, then relations/offers/pools. That is 5 waves and 16 statements per keystroke, measured with the wave-counting adapter, against 2 for a plain list.
confirmed.measured: Live, time to first byte for /api/products?search=X&limit=6: pla 1.07 s, bambu 0.88 s, petg 0.54 s, pl 1.55 s. Wire size: 9.0, 8.5, 2.9 and 8.9 KB for 6 rows.
confirmed.fix:
Memoise the synonyms per isolate with the pricingInputsFor pattern (30 s TTL, purged on writes), which removes 1 wave. Use the slim card from the payload finding (about −70% of the bytes). Consider caching the vocabulary prefixes per isolate.

Expected: −0.15 to −0.3 s per search result update on a phone.
reasons:
The finding is correct about the code and the cost is real, but small. "Low" is the right rating.

CODE (re-read at 7c7190b):
- `searchProducts` runs `const synonyms = opts.synonyms ?? (await loadSynonyms(db))` (worker/lib/search/store.ts:422). `loadSynonyms` (store.ts:373-380) is a plain `SELECT … FROM search_synonyms LIMIT 5000`.
- The only caller on the shop's path, worker/routes/products.ts:3572, passes no `synonyms`.
- A grep of worker/ finds no per-isolate memo anywhere. The only other readers or writers of the table are the admin routes in adminTaxonomy.ts:1377-1412.
- The synonyms map feeds `expandQuery`, the prefixes and the vocabulary scan, so its read cannot overlap with them.
- The chain for a search that finds something is 5 dependent waves: synonyms → vocabulary range scan (store.ts:479) → postings (store.ts:510) → products together with ctx and idx (products.ts:3732, both memoised) → relations, offers and pools (products.ts:3743). A composition match adds 2 more.
- A plain list is 2 waves. A guest without a cookie has no session read (session.ts:176-177), so there is no hidden extra wave.
- Each prefix is its own edge-cache key (`LISTING_CACHE_PARAMS`). On this low-traffic shop it misses, except for backspacing, which the client's `recent` map and the browser's max-age=60 already cover.
- Nothing else handles this: no srcset-style fallback, no edge rule, no lazy path.

LIVE (114 anonymous GETs from colo IAD; the limit/offset values were varied so every request missed the cache; server time = TTFB minus TLS):
- Edge HIT: 0.07 s.
- `search=!!` (exactly 2 dependent D1 waves, synonyms then the empty-index probe): median 0.166 s, minimum 0.144 s. That is about 48 ms per wave, and at most 37 ms at the minimum.
- `search=zqxjv` (3 waves): median 0.248 s, so the third wave adds about 80 ms.
- `search=pla` (5 waves): median 0.58 s, range 0.38–3.0 s.
- Plain `limit=K` (2 waves): median 0.68 s.
- Live-search requests (limit 4–6) for p, pl, pla, bambu, petg and «بامبو»: 0.33–1.18 s, with 0.43 vs 1.0 s for the same query.
- What this shows: the synonyms round trip is about 40–80 ms, roughly 8–14% of a search miss from IAD. Most of a miss is spent in the heavy products and relations statements, not in the number of waves. A 2-wave plain list is slower than the 5-wave search. Run-to-run noise (±0.5 s) is larger than the cost of one wave. The finding's single numbers (pl 1.55 s, pla 1.07 s) sit inside that noise.
- A dependent D1 query takes 37 ms or less from IAD. That puts the D1 primary in North America (it was created from a GitHub runner without `--location`, DECISIONS row 171).
- So for a phone served from an Iraqi PoP, each wave is probably 0.15–0.2 s. This is inferred; I did not measure from Iraq.

PAYLOAD:
- `search=pla&limit=6` is 57.7 KB of JSON (9.1 KB on the wire).
- `media` alone is 47 KB (81%), `images` 8.3 KB. The panel shows one thumbnail per row, so a slim card is real.
- But only about 6 KB on the wire would be saved, which is minor.

IMPACT ON DISPLAY:
- It never touches FCP or LCP on /, /products, /categories or product pages.
- It only affects the search panel's update after the 200 ms debounce (the previous rows stay visible meanwhile) and the first grid on a /products?search= landing.

FIX NOTES:
- Memoising the synonyms (pricingInputsFor pattern, forgotten by the admin synonym PUT/DELETE) is correct. It only helps keystrokes that land on a warm isolate.
- Vocabulary + postings are 2 more dependent waves. With a catalogue of about 26 listed products, memoising the vocabulary or the whole token index per isolate would bring search down to the plain list's 2 waves. That is a bigger win than the synonyms memo alone, and the finding only mentions it as "consider".

The cause is real, but the finding's measurement does not show it, and only one of the proposed fixes is worth doing.

Code (read-only, 7c7190b):
- loadSynonyms (worker/lib/search/store.ts:373-380) has no per-isolate memo. Its comment says "cached per request", which only means the map is passed in once.
- searchProducts waits on each read before starting the next: synonyms (store.ts:422), then the vocabulary scan (:480), then the postings (:512).
- worker/routes/products.ts then reads products, ctx and idx together (:3732), and after that relations, offers and pools together (:3744). That is 5 dependent waves on a warm isolate.
- Nothing else covers it. anonymousCached (worker/lib/edgePolicy.ts) keys on the raw search string (s-maxage=120), so a new prefix always misses. The client-side `recent` map in LiveSearch.tsx only repaints while the request runs; the request always goes out.
- The finding understates the scope. The results page /products?search= (src/pages/Products.tsx, PAGE_SIZE=50) runs the same 5-wave chain before its grid can paint. So it is on that page's first-display path, not only on the live panel.

Live re-measurement (curl from the IAD colo, one reused connection, cache keys made unique by letter case, about 16 samples per class, medians; scratch files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-livesearch-waves/):

| Request | Waves | Median TTFB |
|---|---|---|
| Edge-cache hit | 0 | 0.058 s |
| Punctuation search (synonyms + probe) | 2 | 0.152 s |
| No-match search (synonyms + vocabulary + probe) | 3 | 0.144 s |
| Plain list, 1-12 rows | 2 | 0.268 s |
| petg | 5 | 0.348 s |
| bambu | 5 | 0.390 s |
| pla (wide one-letter scan) | 5 | 0.388 s |

- Adding a wave from IAD costs about 0 ms (3 waves is no slower than 2). So the D1 primary sits next to IAD. This matches DECISIONS row 171: D1 was created from a GitHub runner without --location.
- So the finding's TTFBs (0.54-1.55 s) are not caused by the waves. They come from Slow-4G emulation, the server building cards, and cold-isolate spikes; I saw spikes of 0.6-1.4 s on 2-wave and 5-wave requests alike.
- Everything search-specific (synonyms, vocabulary, postings, scoring) costs only about 0.08-0.12 s over a plain list from IAD.

Where it does cost a phone user: a shopper in Iraq. The Worker runs at the Iraqi Cloudflare point of presence (PoP), so each dependent wave is one round trip from Iraq to US-East and back. I estimate that at 150-200 ms per wave, but I could not measure it because I have no vantage point in Iraq.

Rating "low" is right. This slows search results and the search results page, not the home, category and product first paint the owner is complaining about.

The proposed fixes, taken one at a time:
1. **Memoise the synonyms per isolate:** worth doing. It removes one wave from every keystroke after the first, because typing keeps hitting the same warm isolate.
2. **Slim card:** negligible. The wire size is 9.1 KB zstd for 6 rows (57.7 KB raw). Cutting about 6 KB saves roughly 10-40 ms even on Slow-4G, and JSON parsing is about 2 ms with the CPU slowed ×4.
3. **Cache vocabulary prefixes per isolate:** misdirected. The prefix changes on almost every keystroke, so few lookups would hit. Two changes would remove a second wave instead: cache the whole small vocabulary per isolate, or read the postings by prefix range in the same statement as the vocabulary.
gains:
- **Synonyms memo:** removes 1 dependent D1 wave per search update, about 40–80 ms measured from IAD (median 48 ms per wave from the `search=!!` 2-wave probe vs edge HIT; +82 ms median for the third wave). For a phone served from an Iraqi PoP it is about 0.15–0.2 s, inferred from the D1 primary being in North America, not measured from Iraq. It only applies to keystrokes on a warm isolate.
- **Slim card:** 57.7 KB raw / 9.1 KB wire becomes about 3 KB wire. That saves about 30 ms at Slow-4G 1.6 Mbps and about 5 ms on real 4G; JSON parsing gains about 2–3 ms on a ×4 CPU.
- **Total:** about 0.07–0.11 s per search update at the lab colo, about 0.15–0.23 s on an Iraqi phone, against a search TTFB of 0.33–1.18 s.
- **No effect on page display:** zero change to FCP or LCP of /, /products, /categories or product pages; only the search panel and a /products?search= landing benefit.
- **Larger option:** a per-isolate vocabulary or index memo would remove 2 more waves, about 0.1–0.15 s from IAD and about 0.3–0.4 s from Iraq.

Measurements are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-search/run1.txt through run4.txt and pla6.json.

Synonyms memo: one dependent D1 wave less per search update, about −0.15 to −0.2 s on a phone in Iraq. That is an estimate of the Iraq to US-East round trip, not a measurement. From IAD I measured the wave at about 0 ms (3-wave no-match search median 0.144 s vs 2-wave search 0.152 s). It applies from the second keystroke on (warm isolate), and to the /products?search= results page. Slim card: 9.1 → about 3 KB on the wire, about −0.01 to −0.04 s, which is negligible. Caching the whole vocabulary per isolate, or merging the vocabulary and postings reads, would remove a second wave: about −0.35 to −0.4 s in total per update on an Iraqi phone (same estimate).

confirmed.title: Category and other non-rewritten pages get no head start, so the whole page waits on a chain: entry JS → resolve request → route chunks → catalogue read
confirmed.routes: /categories, /categories/:slug, /categories/:slug/:sub, /community (and every main-site SPA path not in run_worker_first: /bundles, /requests, /compare, /used-printers, /cart, /auth …)
confirmed.cause: wrangler.jsonc:101-131 run_worker_first names only /, /products, /product/*, /bundles/*, /p/*, /community/store/* (plus files and API). Every other document is served by the asset layer as the bare index.html, and assetWithPreview's main-host branch is limited to '/' and '/products' (worker/index.ts:878). routeModuleFor (worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:660-671) knows no catalogue route. So these documents carry no lv-resolve block, no route modulepreload and no data preload. Three costs follow. (1) StoreProvider starts unresolved (src/StoreContext.tsx:119-179) and AppContent returns only <RouteFallback/> — no header, no nav, no page (src/App.tsx:706) — until GET /api/storefront/resolve answers. bootFetch can start that request only at module evaluation (src/lib/bootFetch.ts:195-223), i.e. after the 196 KB entry closure has downloaded. (2) The lazy route (App.tsx:433-435) asks for its static closure only when React renders it after resolve: 28 files for CategoryPage, 26 for CategoryListing, 7 for CategoriesExplorer. (3) The page's own read (/api/catalog/:slug, /api/catalog/tree) leaves only after that chunk mounts.
confirmed.measured:
Live audit (phone medians), LCP: /categories 4096 ms, /categories/printer-accessories 5980 ms, /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials 5992 ms, versus /products 3304 ms, which has the head start. The category documents carry no lv-resolve, preload or modulepreload (diff of the live HTML).

My trace of /categories/printer-accessories (phone):
- resolve 2072→2302 ms
- 31 chunk requests issued at 2459–2467 ms; the last finished at 4002 ms
- blank RouteFallback 2259→4195 ms
- /api/catalog/printer-accessories requested only at 4140 ms (answered 5096)
- LCP 6008–6308 ms

A/B on the live site (same HTML served in the browser with hints added; 3 cold phone runs per variant, medians), LCP:
| route | base | + inline resolve | + route modulepreloads | + data preload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| /categories/printer-accessories | 6164 | 5600 | 5328 | 4344 |
| /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials | 6228 | 5976 | 5900 | 4840 |
| /categories | 4912 | 4316 | 4136 | 3236 |
| /community (resolve + access preload) | 3204 | | | 2888 |
reasons:
The finding is real. Nothing else handles it. I could not refute it, but it is somewhat over-rated, and the proposed fix leaves out one data read on each kind of page.

Code check (7c7190b):
- wrangler.jsonc:101-131 run_worker_first does not list /categories, /categories/* or /community.
- In assetWithPreview, mainOpening covers only '/' and '/products' (worker/index.ts:878).
- routeModuleFor (worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:660-671) knows no catalogue page.
- bootRequests (src/lib/bootFetch.ts:195-223) starts only resolve, /api/home, /products and /product/* reads.
- The StoreProvider gate (src/StoreContext.tsx:119-179) and AppContent (App.tsx:706) work as described.
- The lazy routes are at App.tsx:433-435.
- The only prefetch for catalogue pages is src/lib/catalog/prefetch.ts. It runs on pointerdown or focus of in-app links (CategoryRowBanners, ProductShelf, RelatedCategories, BrandShelf), so it does not help a cold landing.

Live check today:
- The /categories, /categories/printer-accessories, /community and /bundles documents are 2,008 B, no-cache, with 3 modulepreloads and no lv-resolve or fetch preload.
- /products carries lv-resolve, 15 modulepreloads, a fetch preload of /api/products?limit=50, and s-maxage=60.

Timeline on the live phone profile (360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, Slow-4G; scripts and logs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-catchain3/), base /categories/printer-accessories:
- The entry finishes at about 1.94 s.
- Resolve runs 2.05-2.41 s.
- The 28 route chunks are requested at 2.37-2.47 s and finish at 3.99-4.32 s.
- /api/catalog/printer-accessories runs 4.05-4.62 s.
- /api/products?category=cat_pacc runs 4.50-5.03 s.
- LCP is at 5.3-5.6 s.

Corrections:
1. The 'no header, no nav' frame lasts only one resolve round trip, about 0.3 s. After that the Header paints at about 2.4-2.5 s. What stays black until about 4.5 s is the routed area (the in-shell RouteFallback, App.tsx:905). The user still sees no content.
2. The proposed data preload names only /api/catalog/<slug> or /api/catalog/tree. The listing read needs the category id, which comes from the first answer, so it stays chained: on the fdm page it is still requested at 3.70 s with the fix. On /categories the LCP banner photo comes from /api/products?sort=available&limit=50 (the photo pool), which the fix does not name either.
3. The fix has costs:
   - The 26-28 modulepreloads compete with the entry. The entry finished 150-350 ms later (1.94 → 2.10-2.32 s) and the shell painted about 100 ms later on printer-accessories.
   - Moving the documents to run_worker_first costs about 20 ms of time to first byte (TTFB). I measured it with curl: /products 154 ms against /categories 131-138 ms.
   Both costs are small next to the gain.
4. 'Critical' overstates it. Only cold landings pay this cost: search results, shared links and reloads. In-app moves to these pages are already prefetched on pointerdown. For a cold landing on a category page, though, it is the largest single wait. I would rate it high.

A cheaper partial alternative: start the page's catalogue read in bootRequests at module evaluation (about 2.0 s instead of about 4.0 s). That needs no Worker change. An earlier skeptic run (skeptic-catchain2, the cat+list variant) got most of the LCP gain from the data preloads alone.

This is a real cause and it is still live. I could not refute it. The gain on the two deep category pages is about what the finding says. It is overstated for /categories, the proposed fix leaves out one read there, and "critical" is a bit high.

CODE (re-read at 7c7190b; the current default head changes none of these files except two unrelated import-route additions):
- wrangler.jsonc:101-131: run_worker_first contains no /categories and no /community except /community/store/*.
- worker/index.ts:878: mainOpening covers only '/' and '/products'.
- worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:660-671: routeModuleFor knows no catalogue page.
- src/lib/bootFetch.ts:195-223: bootRequests starts resolve only once the entry module runs. It starts catalogue reads only for /products and /product/*.
- src/App.tsx:706: `if (!resolved) return <RouteFallback />`. RouteFallback (App.tsx:113-139) is an empty black min-h-dvh div; only the AppIntro mascot paints behind it.
- The lazy pages are at App.tsx:433-435. The page reads start inside them: loadCategory → /api/catalog/:slug (src/lib/catalog/data.ts:44); loadTree (CategoryListing.tsx:50-57); the photo pool /api/products?sort=available&limit=50 (data.ts:58-61, CategoriesExplorer.tsx:75).
- Nothing else covers this. The live document headers have an Early Hints Link for the CSS and the font only.

LIVE CHECKS (curl, at two successive deploys, entries index-Cc0wdnnC and index-oWU6EvxE):
- /categories, /categories/printer-accessories, /community and /bundles carry no lv-resolve, no route modulepreload and no fetch preload. /products carries all three.
- The route closures in the live manifest: CategoryPage 28 files, 67 KB wire; CategoryListing 26 files, 61 KB; CategoriesExplorer 7 files, 25 KB. The entry closure is 184 KB.
- Cost of serving these documents through the Worker: none measurable. Over 12 interleaved samples each, TTFB minus connect was 0.13-0.15 s both for the Worker-rewritten / and /products and for the asset-layer /categories pages.

MY OWN A/B (Playwright; phone 360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, Slow-4G 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps; cold; the live document rewritten in the browser only):
- /categories/printer-accessories:
  - base median 5920 ms (6 runs)
  - + inline resolve: 5580
  - + resolve + route modulepreload: 5640
  - + resolve + catalog preload, no modulepreload: 5116
  - + resolve + modulepreload + /api/catalog/printer-accessories preload: 4530 (6 runs), so −1.4 s
  - Content paint moved from about 5.2-5.9 s to 3.9-4.2 s.
- /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials:
  - base 5476
  - + resolve + modulepreload + tree preload: 4488 (−1.0 s)
  - + the listing read as well: 4224 (−1.25 s)
  - One base run took 8664 ms because the resolve round trip alone took 1.5 s. The gate also makes network hiccups worse.
- /categories:
  - base 4684 (5 runs)
  - + resolve + modulepreload + tree, i.e. the fix as proposed: 3992 (−0.7 s)
  - adding the photo-pool preload: 3560 (−1.1 s)
- /community:
  - base 3176
  - + resolve: 2796
  - + resolve + /api/community/access preload: 2680 (−0.4 to −0.5 s)

CORRECTIONS:
1. The finding's −1.7 s on /categories does not hold for the fix it proposes; I measured −0.7 s. The LCP banner waits on the photo-pool read /api/products?sort=available&limit=50 (26.7 KB wire, 160 KB JSON), and the fix should preload that read too.
2. The route modulepreloads gain nothing on their own (RM vs R, about 0). On Slow-4G they share the link with the 184 KB entry and push the shell back about 250 ms. They pay only together with the data preload: RMD was 0.77 s faster than RD in the same batch.
3. On printer-accessories and listing pages, the listing read /api/products?category=<id>&facets=1&limit=24 is one more step after the catalog read. The Worker cannot name <id> without a lookup. In my runs it was worth 0 to 0.26 s.
4. The cost hits only cold document loads of these URLs: a landing from search or a shared link, or a refresh. In-app navigation never pays it. Rate it "high", not "critical".
5. Wrangler's negative patterns could replace path-by-path listing: "/*" in run_worker_first plus "!/assets/*" and similar exclusions.

Note: I ran one `git fetch -q` in /home/user/levonis-perf to compare against the current head. It touched only remote-tracking refs: no checkout, no edits. Logs and scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-headstart/ (pacc.log, pacc2.log, fdm.log, cats3.log, comm.log, tools/ab.mjs).
gains:
Phone, cold landing, my A/B on the live site. The proposal was applied exactly (inline resolve, modulepreload of the route closure, route CSS as preload-as-style, one data preload), plus 25 ms on the document for the Worker. LCP:
- /categories/printer-accessories: 5470 → 4522 ms (−0.95 s, medians, 2 runs each). Content (the data-page element) 4649 → 3659 ms. Adding a listing preload: 4294 ms (−1.2 s).
- /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials (1 run each): 7672 → 5300 ms. The base run was inflated by a slow 1.3 s tree read; against the audit median of 5992 ms it is about −0.7 s. With a listing preload: 5216 ms.
- /categories (1 run each): 5508 → 4124 ms (−1.4 s). With a photo-pool preload: 3488 ms.
- FCP: −0.3 to +0.1 s, and the shell paints about 0.1 s later on printer-accessories, because the entry arrives 0.15-0.35 s later behind the modulepreloads.

My estimate: about −0.8 to −1.4 s LCP on cold phone loads of category pages as proposed. Naming the second data read (the listing by category id, or the photo pool on /categories) adds about −0.1 to −0.6 s more. The claimed −1.4 to −1.8 s is the upper end. On /community I expect about −0.3 s (one resolve round trip), which I did not re-measure. In-app moves gain nothing (they are already prefetched).

Phone LCP on a cold landing (medians, live site, Slow-4G + CPU x4):
- /categories/:slug about −1.4 s (5.92 → 4.53 s)
- /categories/:slug/:sub about −1.0 s (5.48 → 4.49 s), or −1.25 s with the listing read added
- /categories −0.7 s as proposed (4.68 → 3.99 s), or −1.1 s if the photo pool /api/products?sort=available&limit=50 is preloaded too
- /community −0.4 to −0.5 s (3.18 → 2.68 s)
- Every other main-host SPA document gains about −0.2 to −0.4 s of shell paint from the inline resolve alone, more when the resolve round trip is slow (seen at 0.7-1.5 s).
- Moving these documents to Worker-first costs no measurable TTFB.
- In-app navigation gains nothing.

confirmed.title: Category pages run their reads one after another, and the explorer's banner photos wait for 50 products plus the whole /api/home
confirmed.cause:
Three serial reads:
- CategoryListing renders ListingSkeleton until /api/catalog/tree has mapped slug → id (CategoryListing.tsx:44-98). Only then does ListingView mount, and useListing (src/components/listing/useListing.ts:64-72) issues /api/products?category=<id>.
- CategoryPage shows its skeleton until /api/catalog/:slug answers (CategoryPage.tsx:124). In listing layout (CategoryPage.tsx:148-160) it then mounts ListingView, which fetches the same category's products a second time.
- CategoriesExplorer (CategoriesExplorer.tsx:73-94) builds its banner photos from loadPhotoPool(): /api/products?sort=available&limit=50 (src/lib/catalog/data.ts:56-64). It also calls fetchGradedStock, which downloads the entire /api/home just to read open_box (src/lib/api.ts:1958-1961). The banners (the LCP) get their photos only after the pool settles.
confirmed.measured:
Phone traces:
- fdm listing: /api/catalog/tree 4537→4732 ms; /api/products?category=cat_materials_fdm only at 4944 → 5773 ms (19.6 KB); card images at 5949 ms; LCP 6484 ms.
- printer-accessories: /api/catalog/printer-accessories 4140→5096 ms; /api/products?category=cat_pacc&facets=1&limit=24 at 5556→6140 ms; product grid complete at 6605 ms.
- /categories: /api/products?sort=available&limit=50 (27.3 KB wire, 160 KB JSON) and /api/home (11.3 KB wire, 47 KB JSON) at 3430→4450 ms; first banner photo requested at 4504 ms; LCP 5424 ms.

In the A/B, firing these reads from the document in parallel cut LCP a further 0.9–1.06 s on top of the chunk preloads (5328→4344, 5900→4840, 4136→3236).
confirmed.fix:
- Let the listing ask by slug (the server resolves slug → id), or have /api/catalog/:slug return the first listing page it already reads, so the page needs one request, not two.
- Put one photo per root/child in /api/catalog/tree, so the explorer draws its banners from the tree.
- Load the 50-product pool, /api/home and /api/bundles after LCP, or drop them.

Expected gain: 0.4–1.0 s LCP on phone category pages (measured upper bound above).
reasons:
The finding is real for the two listing routes. For /categories it is overstated, and the A/B gain it quotes belongs to a different fix.

1) CategoryListing (/categories/:slug/:sub) is a true two-step chain.
- CategoryListing.tsx:52/58 asks for /api/catalog/tree. Line 98 shows ListingSkeleton until the tree has answered.
- Only then does ListingView mount. useListing.ts:69 then asks for /api/products?category=<id>.
- Measured live (phone 360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, Slow-4G, cold): base runs had tree 3917-4205 then products 4367-4688, and tree 4012-4599 then products 4750-5504.
- My A/B started the products read at the same moment as the tree (scratchpad .../perf/skeptic-catserial/ab.mjs, run-fdm.log). LCP went 5820→5164 and 6352→5432. Median 6086→5298, about -0.79 s, n=2.
- A client-only fix is possible: /api/products already resolves a slug (worker/routes/products.ts:3482 `WHERE id = ?1 OR slug = ?1`).
- When the visitor arrives from /categories inside the app, the tree is already cached (pageCache, 5 min). So this hop only costs on deep-link or cold landings.

2) CategoryPage (/categories/:slug, listing layout) is also real.
- CategoryPage.tsx:78 loads the category. Line 124 shows the skeleton until it answers. Line 148 then mounts ListingView, which asks for the products again.
- The catalog payload already carries the same 2 cards (shelf ids = listing ids prd_174dda…, prd_1f336f…). So the cards are downloaded twice.
- A/B: products ready 5089→4524, LCP 5560→5240 (-0.32 s, n=1).
- The live-1 traces put the possible data head start at about 0.44-0.66 s.
- The pointerdown prefetch (prefetch.ts) only warms /api/catalog/:slug, so this hop also happens on in-app navigation.

3) /categories is mis-described and mis-rated.
- These reads are not serial. CategoriesExplorer.tsx:69 and :75-83 start tree, pool, /api/home and /api/bundles in the same commit.
- Live-1: the pool finished 100 ms BEFORE the tree in run 1 and +125 ms after it in run 2. In my base runs it finished +178 and +159 ms after the tree.
- /api/home only feeds the "used" extra banner below the roots. It does not hold any first-screen photo; it only shares bandwidth (9.4 KB wire).
- A/B emulating "photo in the tree" (pool served the instant the tree lands, home and bundles held back): the raw median went 4986→4414. But most of that is chunk-timing noise: jsEnd was 3763/3381 in base and 3435/3007 in the variant.
- Measured from when the tree request starts, the banner image request was only 70-120 ms earlier and LCP only 30-230 ms earlier. About 0.1-0.2 s, not 0.4-1.0 s.
- The pool does return the whole shop (26 products, 26 KB wire, 168 KB JSON), but on this route it is concurrent with the tree, not ahead of it.

4) The "0.9-1.06 s" A/B figure measures a different fix.
- It comes from preloading the FIRST read from the HTML document so it starts before the route chunks load. That is the separate head-start finding.
- Once that preload exists, also preloading the second read added little. In earlier skeptic runs (catchain3 prop→prop+x) it gave -84 ms on fdm and -228 ms on printer-accessories. In headstart RMD→RMDL it gave no gain (4696→4812).
- So the two gains cannot be added together.

On the proposed fix: "ask by slug" and "fire the listing read alongside the catalog read" are right. If /api/catalog/:slug embeds the first page instead, keep in mind that this response is cached by path only (catalog.ts ignores the query). The embedded page could therefore only serve a URL with no filters or sort. Moving photos into the tree is a small win, worth doing mainly to drop the 26 KB pool.

The finding is real, but it is rated too high for /categories, and its headline A/B number measures a different fix from the one it proposes.

CODE (re-read at 7c7190b):
- CategoryListing.tsx:98 returns ListingSkeleton until loadTree() resolves. Only then does ListingView mount, and useListing.ts:64-72 asks /api/products?category=<id>.
- The page cache (src/lib/pageCache.ts) is a Map in module scope. It is empty on every cold load, so a deep link always pays the wait.
- CategoryPage.tsx:124 waits for /api/catalog/:slug. In layout 'listing' (lines 148-165), ListingView then reads the same products again. It has no prop to take initial data, so it shows ProductGridSkeleton until that read answers.
- Nothing already handles this. bootFetch.ts primes only resolve, /api/home and /products. App.tsx:245-250 primes data on a tap only for /products and /product/. prefetch.ts:30-33 warms only /api/catalog/:slug, so an in-app tap into a listing-layout category still pays the second read.
- New evidence the finding missed (live curl): 4 of the 6 root categories use the listing layout: printers, printer-accessories, maintenance-parts and used. In every one, the /api/catalog/:slug answer already carries all of the department's products: 3/3, 2/2, 1/1 and 1/1. The second read only adds facets and the total. A client-only fix is enough: draw the first cards from payload.shelves and let the listing read fill in the facets. No server change is needed.
- Explorer: the live tree has no admin pictures (no hero_image_url or image_url on any node), so every banner photo comes from the 50-product pool.

LIVE A/B (my own run; phone 360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, Slow-4G 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps, cold context):
- Method: no page.route was used. The variant 'dep' is a fetch wrapper in an init script. It starts the listing read at the moment the page asks its first read and answers the page's own later call from that response. This reproduces only the proposed fix. It does not start anything earlier than the page already does.
- printer-accessories: LCP median 5582 → 5218 ms. Measured from the start of the first read, per run: −354 ms (catalog 566 ms, listing a cache miss at 1006 ms) and −79 ms (both reads edge HITs, about 250 ms).
- fdm listing: LCP median 6272 → 5524 ms. Per run: −1092 ms (tree a miss at 1194 ms) and +199 ms (in that run the dep variant's own listing read was the slow one, 837 ms).
- Cache cost (curl): the first curl of each read after its edge copy expired took catalog/printers 1.39 s, products?category=cat_printers 1.2 s, pacc listing 0.88 s and the pool 0.52 s of server time. A HIT costs about 0.07-0.1 s. The edge TTLs are short (catalog/:slug max-age=60, listing s-maxage=120, tree 300) and are kept per Cloudflare location, so on a low-traffic shop most real visitors will hit a miss. The chained cost is about the shorter of the two reads plus a 115-220 ms render gap on CPU x4: roughly 0.3 s with warm caches and roughly 0.8-1.3 s with cold ones.

MIS-RATED PARTS:
1. The quoted A/B gain of 0.9-1.06 s came from starting the reads from the document. That also skips the route-chunk wait: the tree only starts at 3.8-4.4 s in my traces. The proposed fixes (listing by slug, catalog answer carrying page 1, photos in the tree) do not do that. To get that number you would also have to prime /api/catalog/tree or /api/catalog/:slug in bootFetch, the way /products is primed.
2. /categories: the pool, /api/home and /api/bundles already start on mount, at the same time as the tree (CategoriesExplorer.tsx:73-89). The banners' words are drawn as soon as the tree arrives; only the photos wait. The pool holds back the LCP photo only when it finishes after the tree:
   - live-1: the pool finished before the tree (3905 vs 4005 ms), so no delay.
   - The earlier skeptic run: 159-178 ms.
   - Worst case (tree HIT 0.17 s, pool MISS 0.61 s): about 0.45 s.
3. /api/home (fetchGradedStock) is never on the LCP path. It is an 11 KB edge HIT that only feeds the 'used' banner below the fold, about 55 ms of link time. Negligible.

Verdict: real, worth about high-medium. The biggest and cheapest win is on the listing-layout category pages (4 of 6 roots, on cold loads and in-app taps), and the sub-listings on cold loads. The /categories part is minor.

- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-catserial-c/run-pacc.log

- live JSON in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-catserial-c/dl/
gains:
Cold landing on a listing-layout category page, phone (Slow-4G, CPU x4), measured live with A/B:
- fdm sub-listing: LCP -0.66 s and -0.92 s (median 6086→5298 ms, n=2); products data ready 0.5-1.1 s earlier.
- printer-accessories: LCP -0.32 s (5560→5240, n=1); products data ready 0.57 s earlier.

/categories explorer (photo from the tree, pool, home and bundles deferred):

If the document head-start preload ships first, this fix adds only about 0.1-0.25 s.

My estimate: 0.3-0.9 s LCP on cold listing pages, about 0.1-0.2 s on /categories, and 0 on in-app navigation into a sub-listing (the tree is already cached).

My estimate is for the proposed fix alone, measured live on the phone profile (cold context, n=2 per variant).

Listing-layout category pages (printers, printer-accessories, maintenance-parts, used) and sub-listings (for example fdm-materials):
- 0.1-0.35 s off LCP when both reads are edge HITs.
- About 0.8-1.3 s earlier product data when the first read misses the cache, which is the usual case at this traffic level.
- Measured LCP medians: printer-accessories 5582 → 5218 ms (−364 ms); fdm 6272 → 5524 ms (−748 ms).

/categories (photos in the tree, pool deferred):

The 0.9-1.06 s in the finding needs one more change: starting the reads from the document (prime /api/catalog/tree and /api/catalog/:slug in bootFetch).

confirmed.title: The product page must download ~90 KB gzip of route code, including the full motion bundle, before its first pixel
confirmed.cause: Product.tsx statically imports panels that the first paint does not draw: ShippingConflictDialog (:42), ConditionPanel (:83), StockAlertPanel (:84) and QuickBuyBar (:100). src/components/ui/Note.tsx:21 imports `motion` from 'motion/react' (the full proxy), which drags all of vendor-motion (16 KB gzip) into the route's static closure. The worker modulepreloads all 25 files beside the entry (worker/lib/socialPreview.ts chunkPreloads), so they share the 1.6 Mbps link with the entry. Nothing on the route renders until the whole closure has been evaluated.
confirmed.measured:
- Live audit, FCP: 3468 ms on the product page (phone median) versus 2292–2556 ms on every other route; LCP 4284 ms.
- My traces: 32 JS files, 362 KB on the wire, before any product content. The closure's last file (vendor-motion, 18.8 KB) finishes at 3307 ms; the fallback holds until 3372–3495 ms; FCP 3432–3568 ms.
- Build (hashes identical to live): Product chunk 39.8 KB gzip (Product.tsx 148.6 KB raw, StockAlertPanel 21.4 KB, QuickBuyBar 14.2 KB, ConditionPanel 8.2 KB, ShippingConflictDialog 4.5 KB raw); vendor-motion 16.0 KB gzip, reached only via Note.tsx; vendor-icons 13.6 KB gzip; 89.9 KB gzip beyond the entry in total.
confirmed.fix:
- React.lazy StockAlertPanel (only when out of stock), ConditionPanel (graded items), ShippingConflictDialog (on open) and QuickBuyBar (after first paint).
- Switch Note.tsx to `m` plus the existing LazyMotion features (src/lib/motionFeatures.tsx), so vendor-motion leaves the closure.

Expected: ~35–45 KB gzip less before first paint, about −0.2 s FCP/LCP on Slow-4G, and less parse on a ×4 CPU.
reasons:
NOT REFUTED. The cause is real, and I measured it on the live site. Two parts of the finding are wrong: it overstates the bytes, and one of the four proposed deferrals targets something that is drawn on screen.

What I checked again:
- **The live site was redeployed after the audit, but the cause is still there.** The new files are index-oWU6EvxE.js and Product-BRPeh8Sn.js. The Product chunk is now 140 KB raw and 43.5 KB gzip. The live Note chunk (Note-BR8R_Cug.js) still starts with `import{m as p}from"./vendor-motion-DDNunUBr.js"`.
- **Note is the only path into vendor-motion.** I scanned every mirrored chunk. In the Product closure, Note is the only static importer of vendor-motion. The others (PriceRequestPanel, ProductKnowledgeTabs, Tabs, motionFeaturesBundle) are lazy.
- **The page still preloads vendor-motion.** The live HTML of /product/esun-pla-plus modulepreloads 27 route files, and vendor-motion is 25th. This comes from worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:701-731 (chunkPreloads, which preloads the whole closure on purpose).
- **Nothing on this route counts as a first paint until the closure has run.** Header.tsx:152 renders only on `/`. BottomNav is hidden on /product/*. The RouteFallback (App.tsx:113-139) draws no text or image. FCP therefore lands about 40 ms after the fallback is removed. That explains why this route paints about 1 s later than routes that paint the shell.
- **Nothing elsewhere already handles it.** There is no lazy wrapper, edge rule or later srcset that takes vendor-motion off this path.

Live A/B test:
- Setup: phone 360×800, DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G (150 ms, 1.6 Mbps), cold cache, 10 interleaved pairs. Both arms served the same two small intercepted responses (the document and the Note chunk) with the same fixed delays. Everything else came from the live site through the throttle.
- Arm B made one change only: vendor-motion's modulepreload was removed, and Note drew a plain div, which is what `m.div` gives.
- In arm A, vendor-motion is the last file of the closure to arrive (median 3230 ms), and the fallback holds until 3492 ms.
- Results, A → B (medians):

| Metric | A | B | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fallback removed | 3492 ms | 3259 ms | −233 ms |
| FCP | 3530 ms | 3312 ms | −218 ms |
| h1 shown | 3775 ms | 3569 ms | −206 ms |
| LCP | 4256 ms | 4048 ms | −208 ms |
| JS before FCP | 338 KB | 305 KB | −33 KB |

- Arm B is realistic, not best-case. Even in B, vendor-motion is still fetched at about 2.5 s by the busy-overlay features bundle, and the gain held anyway.

Where the finding is wrong:
1. **Bytes.** It claims 35–45 KB gzip can come off. The real figure is about 25–27 KB gzip:
   - vendor-motion is 16.0 KB gzip (18.8 KB on the wire).
   - The four panels are inlined in the Product chunk. Minified and gzipped on their own they are 12.2 KB: StockAlertPanel 5.6, QuickBuyBar 3.0, ConditionPanel 2.3, ShippingConflictDialog 1.4. Inside the chunk they save less, about 9–11 KB.
   - Almost all of the roughly 0.2 s gain comes from Note.tsx alone.
2. **QuickBuyBar is drawn on the first screen.** The finding says the first paint does not draw it. For a signed-in viewer of a catalogue product it is the purchase bar itself (Product.tsx:3891 `showQuickBuyToggle = isAuthenticated && source === 'catalog'`, rendered at :3895). Guests never render it. Loading it "after first paint" would make the main buy button appear late, all for about 3 KB (about 15 ms). Either drop it from the fix, or lazy-load it with the plain button (:3913-3923) as the fallback.
3. **Note fix.** The product page's only Note (Product.tsx:2923) uses `animate={false}`, so an `m.div` draws in its final state without any motion features. Note has 15 importers, though, and the ones that animate need `<MotionFeatures>` (src/lib/motionFeatures.tsx) around them or they stay at opacity 0.
4. **Severity.** Medium is right: about 5% of the phone LCP on the page shared links land on. On desktop the effect is negligible.

My harness is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-productclosure/scripts/ab.mjs. The raw results are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-productclosure/ab.jsonl.

The cause is real, but the finding overstates its size. Most of the gain comes from one file, Note.tsx, and the comparison with other routes that the finding uses as evidence does not hold.

Checked on the live site today. Live now runs head 5cf99a3f, not 7c7190b. Step 7 changed Product.tsx, but the static imports the finding names are still there, at lines 42, 87, 88 and 104 on that head. I exported 5cf99a3f into scratch and ran `vite build`. The hashes match live exactly (Product-BRPeh8Sn.js, index-oWU6EvxE.js), and the rewritten document in my lab has the same 27 modulepreload lines as live.
- The route closure beyond the entry is 24 files, 94.1 KB gzip -9. The entry's own closure is 183.1 KB.
- Note-BR8R_Cug.js is the only chunk that statically imports vendor-motion: `import{m as p}from"./vendor-motion-DDNunUBr.js"`, from src/components/ui/Note.tsx:21 `import { motion } from 'motion/react'`. vendor-motion is 16.0 KB gzip and is the 25th of the 27 preload lines, so it finishes last.
- Nothing else already handles this. The motion-features prefetch waits for load, fonts and images (src/lib/afterCriticalPaint.ts), so it does not compete with this download. The worker's whole-closure preload was a measured, deliberate choice (PERFORMANCE_LOG P2b) and is not itself the fault.

What the finding gets wrong:
1. **Bytes.** I built the proposed fix in scratch: Product, ConditionPanel, StockAlertPanel and QuickBuyBar via React.lazy, and Note switched to `m` under MotionFeatures.
   - The route closure drops from 94.1 to 67.9 KB, a saving of 26.3 KB, not the claimed 35–45 KB.
   - The Product chunk goes from 43.8 to 33.9 KB; the panels become chunks of their own of 1.4, 2.2, 3.5 and 5.8 KB.
   - The Note change alone drops the closure to 78.1 KB, a saving of 16.0 KB.
2. **Evidence.** "FCP 3468 vs 2292–2556 on every other route" compares different things:
   - Header renders only on '/' (src/components/Header.tsx:152) and BottomNav is hidden on /product/*. On other routes FCP is the shell; on the product page it is the page itself.
   - Product LCP (4284 ms) is in line with /categories (4096) and below the category pages (~5980).
   - So the closure does not explain a 1 s gap. It explains about 0.1–0.3 s.
3. **Where the gain comes from.** The Product chunk already arrives early (done at about 1.96 s). The critical path is the last closure file (about 2.65 s), which is vendor-motion. Moving the panels out of the Product chunk therefore adds little.

**Lab A/B.** A local HTTP/2 server served each build together with the live document, rewritten with that build's preloads; APIs and images were replayed from live. Playwright ran at 360×800, DPR 3, Slow-4G (150 ms, 1.6 Mbps), CPU ×4, cold cache, alternating arms.
- Control (unchanged build), n=15: FCP 2880, LCP 4128, heading 3508 ms. The live audit measured 3468 / 4284.
- Full fix, 15 paired runs:
  - FCP: −120 ms median, −125 mean
  - LCP: −140 median, −173 mean
  - Heading in the DOM: −213 median
  - LCP improved in 13 of 15 pairs.
- Note.tsx alone, n=7: FCP −200, LCP −292, heading −304 ms. That is the same as the full fix within noise.

**Corrections to the proposed fix:**
- Lead with the one-file Note.tsx change.
- `m.div` needs MotionFeatures only when `animate` is true. It also needs the `useMotionFeaturesFailed` fallback, or a note with `initial` opacity 0 stays invisible if the features chunk fails to load.
- QuickBuyBar only renders when `isAuthenticated && source==='catalog'`, so guests already never draw it. Lazy-loading it saves bytes for guests, but for a signed-in user it needs a same-size fallback such as the plain button, or the buy bar pops in late.
- Lazy StockAlertPanel and ConditionPanel would pop in on the products that show them, and they add only about 10 KB.
- Severity is medium-low: about 3–5% of a phone user's LCP on this route.

Scratch files:

- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-productclosure-b/ab2.json
- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-productclosure-b/tools/ab.mjs
- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-productclosure-b/tools/server.mjs
gains: The Note.tsx:21 change alone (motion → m, so vendor-motion leaves the product closure and the worker's preload list) was measured on live at phone Slow-4G with CPU ×4, 10 pairs, medians: FCP −218 ms (3530 → 3312), LCP −208 ms (4256 → 4048), fallback removed −233 ms, and 33 KB less JS before FCP. Lazy-loading StockAlertPanel, ConditionPanel and ShippingConflictDialog would add about 8–9 KB gzip, worth roughly another 40–50 ms on Slow-4G; this part is estimated, not measured. QuickBuyBar is only about 3 KB (about 15 ms) and is the first-screen buy bar for signed-in users, so it should stay or get a fallback. In the A/B lab of the live build (phone 360×800, DPR 3, Slow-4G 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms, CPU ×4, cold cache; n=15 paired runs) it gave FCP −0.12 s, LCP −0.14 to −0.17 s and heading −0.21 s, with LCP better in 13 of 15 pairs.
