confirmed.title: Lazy routes always flash the blank fallback, and React 19 then holds the page back another 300 ms, even when the chunks are already downloaded
confirmed.routes: /products, /product/:slug, every lazy route (and all category routes once their chunks are modulepreloaded)
confirmed.cause: Every storefront page except Home is React.lazy, including the prefetchable() ones (src/App.tsx:157-171, 293-297). A lazy component always suspends on its first render, even when import() targets already-modulepreloaded files, so the first commit is the Suspense fallback (App.tsx:905, RouteFallback = blank min-h-dvh). React 19.2.8 then throttles every retry-lane commit until 300 ms after the last fallback commit: `globalMostRecentFallbackTime + 300 - now()`, labelled "Throttled" (node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js:10793).
confirmed.measured: /products on phone, 2 runs: all 12 route chunks (modulepreloaded by the document) were downloaded by 2494 / 3250 ms; the fallback committed at 2436 / 3120 ms; the page appeared only at 2813 / 3431 ms. That is 377 / 311 ms of blank content area, of which at least 300 ms is React's reveal throttle. FCP that run was 2504 ms; LCP 3664 ms.
confirmed.fix:
Before the first render, resolve the current route's module when the document has modulepreloaded it: in main.tsx, await the route's preload(); the bytes are already there. Make prefetchable() keep the settled module and render `mod.default` directly, without React.lazy, once loaded. No Suspense then happens on the first frame.

Expected: about −0.3 s to content on /products and the other prefetchable routes, and the same on category routes after the document fix.
reasons:
The finding is real. I re-measured it on the live site and re-read the code, and the mechanism holds. The size of the gain is mostly right for when the grid of cards appears, but it is not shown for LCP on a cold visit. The proposed fix also has a cost the finding does not mention.

Code, checked against react@19.2.8 / react-dom@19.2.8 in node_modules:
- **Every lazy route suspends on its first render.** `lazyInitializer` (react.production.js:264-281) calls `import()`, marks the module as pending and throws the promise. `resolveLazy` (react-dom-client.production.js:3254-3262) turns that into a SuspenseException. The first render from `createRoot().render` (main.tsx) runs in DefaultLane, so React renders it synchronously (sync render) and unwinds to the fallback. The first commit is therefore always `RouteFallback` (App.tsx:905). This includes the `prefetchable()` routes (App.tsx:157-172, 293-297), which are plain `React.lazy` underneath.
- **The 300 ms hold is real.** react-dom-client.production.js:10792-10820 holds a finished retry render until `Mn+300-now`. That is a retry-lane render with status 3 (completed), not only one that suspended again. The same code is in the live chunk vendor-react-BDQZ98fV.js as `(e&62914560)===e&&(u=Mn+300-ae(),10<u)`, scheduled through `setTimeout(Js.bind(...))`.
- **Worse than the finding says.** Lines 9706-9712 reset the clock when any boundary's fallback appears or disappears. App.tsx:617-618 wraps the lazy `AppIntro` in its own `<Suspense fallback={null}>`, so the two reveals can push each other back. I saw this happen: in one warm run on /products React held the commit twice (a 117 ms wait was cancelled, then another 136 ms wait ran), and the fallback stayed for 617 ms.
- **Not handled elsewhere.** `bootFetch` starts `/api/products?limit=50` before React mounts, and the document preloads it as a fetch. So the data is usually back before the page commits, which puts the hold directly on the path to the grid and its image requests. Client-side navigations are not affected: the router keeps the old page during a pending transition.
- **No hidden image wait.** React's "suspensey images" do not apply here: `imgCount` is never incremented in this build.

Live measurement (ab.mjs; logs products-ab.log, products-warm.log and product-warm.log, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-lazythrottle/):
- **Setup.** Real Chromium, 360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G (150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbps). A/B in the same browser: arm B wraps `setTimeout` so React's held commit runs with delay 0. Nothing is written to the site.
- **/products, cold.**
  - Blank route area (fallback in → out): 366 / 347 / 365 / 392 / 413 ms live, against 141 / 99 / 439 ms with the hold removed.
  - Grid of cards committed, measured from the first React commit: live median 552 ms (497, 491, 572, 552, 565), against 269 ms with the hold removed (269, 189, 549).
  - The 549 / 439 run is the one where the chunks arrived more than 300 ms after the fallback, so React did not hold the commit and nothing was saved.
  - Image requests start correspondingly earlier.
  - LCP, measured from the first commit: no measurable gain (median 1156 ms live vs 1170 ms). Two of the three no-hold runs downloaded the LCP image more slowly (878 / 606 ms vs about 510-560 ms) because it now shares the Slow-4G link with the remaining chunk bytes.
- **/products, warm (chunks already cached, which is exactly the finding's "already downloaded" case).** Fallback 367 / 617 ms live vs 255 / 257 ms. Grid −100 / −380 ms. LCP from the first commit 689 / 1073 ms vs 590 / 697 ms.
- **/product/esun-pla-plus, warm.** Fallback 365 / 428 ms vs 289 / 301 ms (about −100 ms). Time to content is within noise at n=2. A cold live run showed five held commits in a row (nested lazy sections plus AppIntro).

Where the finding is wrong or mis-fixed:
1. **"Even when the chunks are already downloaded."** On a cold visit the chunks were not all there at the fallback commit: they finished 140-260 ms after it in my runs (+58 ms in the finding's own run). The full cost shows up on repeat visits.
2. **The proposed fix delays the first paint.** Awaiting the route's `preload()` in main.tsx before the first render holds back the first commit, which is what paints the header and is the current FCP (about fallback +50 ms). It would land at "route ready + render", about +100-250 ms on a cold Slow-4G visit and +400 ms when the chunks are late. That cancels much of the gain.
   - A better fix: when the lazy promise settles, reveal the route with an ordinary update from above the boundary (for example `prefetchable` notifies a small store that a component above `<Suspense>` subscribes to). React does not hold DefaultLane or transition commits (the condition at line 10793 matches only retry lanes), so the header still paints at once.
   - Also take `AppIntro`'s lazy boundary out of the reveal clock, since its reveal resets the 300 ms window for the route.
3. **Category routes.** The cost there applies only after their chunks are modulepreloaded. Today they arrive too late for the hold to apply.

Severity medium is fair. It costs about 0.1-0.3 s of blank content area per document load, and more on repeat visits.

The cause is real, but the finding overstates it. Its claim that "at least 300 ms" is React's throttle is wrong.

What I confirmed in code:
- src/App.tsx:157-171 and 293-297: `prefetchable()` wraps `React.lazy`. React 19.2.8's `lazyInitializer` (node_modules/react/cjs/react.production.js:264-281) calls `.then` on a native Promise, so the first render always throws, even for a module already in cache. The first commit is therefore `RouteFallback` (App.tsx:113-139 and 905): a `min-h-dvh bg-black` block under the visible header.
- The live `vendor-react-BDQZ98fV.js` contains `if((e&62914560)===e&&(u=Mn+300-ae(),10<u)){...a.timeoutHandle=Td(Js.bind(null,...,"Throttled",...),u)}` with `Td=setTimeout`. So a finished retry render waits until 300 ms after the last fallback commit.
- Nothing else handles this:
  - main.tsx renders at once.
  - The suspensey-commit path (`Fy`) never counts images in this build, so it returns null.
  - Products itself has no nested lazy except LiveSearch's `Suspense` with `fallback={null}`.

What is wrong in the finding: the 300 ms window starts at the fallback commit. Chunk resolution, module evaluation and the retry render all happen inside it, so the actual hold is 300 minus (render-ready time minus fallback time). The finding's own numbers fit this: chunks were done 58 / 130 ms after the fallback, and render time comes on top, so the held time was about 100-150 ms, not 300+.

Measured on the live site (scratchpad perf/skeptic-lazythrottle-b/thr.mjs; phone 360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, Slow-4G). Method:
- A `setTimeout` wrapper captures the "bound Js" hold and its delay. The "nothrottle" arm sets that delay to 0, only inside my browser.
- A devtools-hook commit log identifies which commit removed the route fallback.

Results:
- Route-reveal holds on live: 122, 137, 61, 180 and 90 ms (warm /products); 94 ms (warm /product); 65, 21 and 45 ms (cold /products, the last two after cancelled holds of 243/163 and 143/118 ms).
- Cascades: another shell `Suspense` reveal re-arms the window (commit at 919 ms with the fallback still shown, next hold computed from about 907 ms), and state updates cancel and redo the held commit. This raised the cost to about 250 ms (/products warm run 1) and about 400 ms (/product warm run 1, reveal +617 vs +218/+205 ms).
- The "already downloaded" claim holds: in warm runs the route chunk ends at 237-401 ms, the fallback commits at about 700 ms, and the hold still applies.
- A/B on warm /products, 5 pairs, medians, all relative to the fallback commit:

| metric | live | throttle off |
|---|---|---|
| reveal | +376 ms | +284 ms |
| product-image request start | +595 ms | +447 ms |
| LCP (absolute) | 1608 ms | 1484 ms |

- A/B on /product (2 warm pairs): LCP 1832 / 1484 ms live vs 1480 / 1496 ms with the throttle off.

Category routes: their documents do not modulepreload the route chunk, so a cold load probably sees no hold today. On a repeat visit (chunk in HTTP cache) the same mechanism applies; I did not measure that.

On the proposed fix: it works, because the route then commits in the first, non-retry-lane commit. Caveats:
- Bound the await in main.tsx, for example only when the route's closure is modulepreloaded and with a short time limit. Otherwise a slow cold chunk delays the shell's first paint.
- `prefetchable` can hand back a synchronous thenable (`{then(r){r(mod)}}`) once settled. `lazyInitializer` then resolves without suspending.
- Shell lazies (Header.tsx:223, LiveSearch.tsx:440) keep their own throttling, but they no longer gate the route.

I made about 370 anonymous GETs to the site in total.
gains:
My estimate on a phone, measured on live levonis-iq.com (360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G, real Chromium, React's hold removed in-browser):

| Route and cache | Measure | Live | Hold removed | Gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| /products, cold | Grid of cards | median 552 ms after the first commit (n=5) | 269 ms (n=3) | −230 to −280 ms when the chunks arrive within the 300 ms window; 0 when they arrive later (1 of 3 runs) |
| /products, cold | Blank route area | about 365 ms | about 100-140 ms | about −250 ms |
| /products, cold | LCP | 1156 ms after the first commit | 1170 ms | not shown (the image then shares the Slow-4G link with the remaining chunks) |
| /products, warm | Grid | | | −100 / −380 ms |
| /products, warm | LCP | | | −100 / −375 ms |
| /product/:slug, warm | Route fallback | | | about −100 ms (content within noise) |

Overall: about −0.25 s to visible content on prefetchable routes, up to −0.38 s on repeat visits, and an LCP gain between 0 and −0.25 s.

The proposed fix (await `preload()` before the first render) would hand back +0.1 to +0.4 s of first paint (the header and shell). Revealing the route with a normal update instead of React's held retry commit keeps the first paint where it is and keeps the full gain.

On a phone, about −0.1 to −0.15 s to route content and LCP in the typical case, not −0.3 s. This is from the live A/B with the "Throttled" `setTimeout` delay forced to 0:
- Warm /products, 5 pairs, medians: content reveal −92 ms, product-image request start −148 ms, LCP −124 ms.
- Measured holds on the route reveal were 21-190 ms (median about 90 ms).
- When another shell `Suspense` re-arms the window or an update cancels the held commit (2 of 7 warm pairs), the gain was about −0.25 to −0.4 s. On /product, LCP was 1832 ms live vs 1480 ms with the throttle off.
- On cold loads it is smaller, because the chunk wait uses up most of the 300 ms window (holds of 21-65 ms on the route, up to 190 ms in one run).

Severity: low to medium. The finding's "~−0.3 s" is the worst case, not the median.

confirmed.title: Every route pays a 239 KB critical payload, partly code it does not need at boot, before React can paint anything
confirmed.cause:
#root is empty, so the first pixel needs index.css, the entry and its three static vendor chunks. In that closure:
- vendor-motion-core is loaded only because AppBusy (App.tsx:47) and UpdateReadyToast (App.tsx:38) mount empty AnimatePresence wrappers at boot, and useRail imports `animate` statically (src/lib/useRail.ts:52) for a spring that runs only on interaction.
- vendor-i18n is src/translations.ts with all three languages (vite.config.ts:208).
- Home is an eager import (App.tsx:271), so every non-home route also downloads and evaluates the Home code.
confirmed.measured:
- Live payload: index 66.7 KB + vendor-react 79.2 KB + vendor-motion-core 35.6 KB + vendor-i18n 14.3 KB + index.css 43.3 KB = 239 KB wire. On phone traces the last of these finishes at 1.87–2.77 s.
- Main-thread trace of / (×4 CPU): module evaluation 196 ms, then a 407 ms first-render task before FCP.
- Live FCP medians: 2.29–2.56 s on every route.
- Build: vendor-motion-core 32.5 KB gzip; vendor-i18n 11.9 KB gzip (about two thirds unused by any one visitor). Home-only modules are ~20% of the entry's 331 KB rendered source: components/home 31.5 KB, pages/Home 10.9 KB, lib/useRail 10.1 KB, lib/homeLayout 10.1 KB.
confirmed.fix:
- Give AppBusy a CSS-only first frame and import motion when a wait actually shows.
- Lazy-load UpdateReadyToast (it draws nothing on a first visit).
- Dynamic-import `animate` in useRail on the first drag.
- Split translations per language.
- Move Home into its own chunk that only '/' modulepreloads.

Expected: ~50–60 KB less on the critical path, about 0.25–0.3 s at 1.6 Mbps, plus ~60–100 ms less evaluation on ×4.
reasons:
The finding is real, but it overstates the reach ("every route") and part of the proposed fix makes things worse. Nothing else on the site handles it already: no SSR, no inline first frame (the live document's body is just `
`), and nothing loads motion lazily on the boot path. How I checked: - I rebuilt the live code from a copy. The output is byte-identical to production: index-oWU6EvxE.js, index-CHfw9WlM.css, vendor-react-BDQZ98fV, vendor-motion-core-DrluXP5O, vendor-i18n-D3w9Xejm. - Live wire sizes today (zstd): entry 64.6 + vendor-react 77.6 + vendor-motion-core 34.0 + vendor-i18n 12.8 + css 41.8 = 230.8 KB. - I built two variants. B1 takes motion off the boot path. B2 is B1 plus Home in its own chunk plus Arabic-only translations. - Lab setup: a local HTTP/2 replay of the live documents, APIs and images. Each document was rewritten the way the Worker would write it. Phone 360x800, DPR 3, CPU x4, 1.6 Mbps, 150 ms RTT, cold. 7 paired runs per route; all variants render the same screens with no page errors. Code facts: 1. The finding's three importers (AppBusy at App.tsx:47, UpdateReadyToast at App.tsx:38, useRail.ts:52) are not the only ones. src/lib/motionFeatures.tsx:36 imports LazyMotion from 'motion/react', and App.tsx:502 and LiveSearch.tsx:8 import preloadMotionFeatures from that file. Those two imports must become dynamic as well, or vendor-motion-core stays on the boot path. 2. The useRail change has to dynamic-import a small wrapper that has code of its own. `import('motion/react')` pulls in the whole namespace and grew motion-core from 32 to 46 KB gzip. A wrapper that only re-exports `animate` was folded back into the entry by Rollup. 3. Product.tsx, the CategoryPage chunk (CategoryHero, ShelfJumpChips…), Overlay.tsx:80 and the Community chunk import motion themselves. On those routes the 34 KB only moves from the boot set into the route's own set: Product goes 93→127 KB and CategoryPage 65→99 KB. Total bytes do not change. - The Worker preloads nothing for /categories* or /community, so there motion-core becomes a late second-wave request. - On /product, the Worker's preload cap (worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:704, cap = 24) would drop vendor-motion from the list. My lab did not apply the cap, so product results in the lab are a best case. Measured (median of 7 paired diffs, B1 against live): - **/ :** FCP and LCP (the h1) both −260 ms. - **/products :** FCP −196 ms; LCP (an image) roughly unchanged, +100 ms with a lot of noise. - **/community :** LCP −164 ms. - **/categories/printer-accessories :** FCP −192 ms, but LCP +124 ms. - **/product/esun-pla-plus :** FCP −24 ms, LCP +12 ms, so nothing. The "move Home into its own chunk" step is a regression on /. B2's LCP on / is +136 ms against live and about +400 ms against B1. Lazy Home adds a chunk after the entry, and it drags the 14 KB vendor-icons file in with it, because the icons the entry used to carry inline become lazy-shared. The language split plus Home removal is worth only about another −90 ms of FCP on the routes other than /. The cost applies only to cold first visits: assets are cached immutable for a year and the service worker serves repeat visits. The rating should be medium for /, /products and /community, and nothing for the product and category pages, where LCP is the worst. Drop the Home split. Keep the motion-off-boot change, including the motionFeatures and wrapper fixes above.

REAL, BUT OVER-RATED, AND THE PROPOSED FIX IS INCOMPLETE IN THREE PLACES, WITH ONE PART THAT MAKES THINGS WORSE. What I confirmed - Live HTML (re-fetched 11:09 UTC; the site has been redeployed since the audit, but the shell is the same) has an empty `
`. It modulepreloads vendor-react, vendor-i18n and vendor-motion-core. Brotli bodies: entry 62.7 KB, react 75.7, motion-core 33.7, i18n 12.1, css 39.8, about 224 KB. With headers that matches the finding's 239 KB. - The entry pulls exactly 4 symbols from vendor-motion-core: LazyMotion, AnimatePresence, m.div and animate. All of them belong to AppBusy, UpdateReadyToast, motionFeatures and useRail. - The live CPU profile of / at ×4 (shell/profile-_.cpuprofile) puts vendor-motion-core self time at only 9 ms. Why the fix as written does not take motion-core off the critical path 1. src/lib/motionFeatures.tsx:36 imports LazyMotion statically. The file stays in the entry through App.tsx:502 and LiveSearch.tsx:8 (preloadMotionFeatures). Lazy chunks (Overlay, Toast, Segmented) import MotionFeatures from it, so LazyMotion stays in the entry. The loader has to be split from the component. 2. UpdateReadyToast is also imported statically by main.tsx:6 (`watchForUpdates`). Lazy-loading it in App.tsx moves nothing; Vite warns "dynamic import will not move module". The store has to be split out. 3. A plain `import('motion/react')` in useRail creates a vendor-motion and vendor-motion-core circular chunk. At runtime this throws "Cannot access 'Te' before initialization": a blank page on / and the ChunkBoundary error on /product. It needs a one-line re-export pinned to its own manual chunk. 4. tests/busyOverlay.test.ts:453-455 requires AppBusy to stay a static import. The "CSS first frame" approach fits that test; a lazy AppBusy does not. Splitting translations is negligible - LanguageContext.tsx:125 falls back to translations.en for every key. - The language comes from localStorage (LanguageContext.tsx:32), so the Worker cannot preload per language. - Only ckb, about 3 KB br, could be dropped. Bytes, measured on my own builds of 7c7190b (brotli 11; vendor hashes are identical to live) - Entry closure + css today (A): 189.2 KB. - Motion fixes only (F): 158.4 KB, which is −30.8 KB on every route. - Motion fixes plus a lazy Home (E): 147.0 KB. But / then also needs the Home closure, 26.6 KB, which includes vendor-icons at 11.7 KB. So / comes to 173.6 KB: 15 KB more than F. - On /product/:slug and the category listing and category pages, motion-core moves into the route's own closure (Product, Overlay or Sheet, then motionFeatures, then LazyMotion). The totals there fall by only about 10 KB. - The claimed "~50–60 KB less" is really about 31 KB for the motion part, plus about 11 KB from the Home split on routes other than /. Timing: A/B in Chromium - Setup: 360×800 at DPR 3, ×4 CPU, 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps. Local HTTP/2 server, the same live HTML and APIs, the same cached images. Only the JS build differs. 4–6 cold runs per cell, no page errors. - The CPU gain is about 10–35 ms (the FCP − last critical response gap barely changes), not the claimed 60–100 ms. Data in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-critpayload-c/ (ab-AE.log, ab-AFE.log, ab-AF2.log).
gains:
Lab measurement (local HTTP/2 replay of live; 360x800 DPR 3, CPU x4, 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms RTT, cold, n=7 paired). Taking motion off the boot path correctly (my B1: −34 KB gzip from the boot set, 178→144 KB):
- / : FCP and LCP −0.26 s (2.27→2.01 s)
- /products : FCP −0.20 s; LCP about 0
- /community : FCP −0.18 s, LCP −0.16 s
- /categories/* : FCP −0.19 s, but LCP about 0 to +0.12 s
- /product/:slug : 0 (FCP −24 ms, LCP +12 ms)

Adding the per-language translations split plus the Home split (B2) gives FCP −0.23 to −0.36 s on routes other than /, but costs / +0.14 s LCP against live (+0.4 s against B1). The Home split should not be done. Realistic total: about 0.2–0.26 s faster first paint on /, /products and /community for first-time visitors; no gain on product or category LCP. The finding's expected 0.25–0.3 s "on every route" is too high.

The two fixed variants, each against today's build, as median change in first paint / main content on the audit's phone profile (×4 CPU, Slow-4G 1.6 Mbps):

| Route | Motion fixes only (F), Home stays eager | Motion fixes + lazy Home (E) |
|---|---|---|
| / | −128 / −128 ms (the hero is earlier) | −148 / **+116 ms** (the hero is later) |
| /products | −104 / −60 ms | −240 / −288 ms (−236 / −230 in a second round) |
| /categories | not measured | −298 / −348 ms |
| /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials | −196 / +52 ms (images bound content at ~5.1 s) | −252 / −104 ms |
| /community | −128 / −74 ms | −212 / −198 ms |
| /product/:slug | about 0 within noise (−82 / −496 in one round, +68 / +100 in the other) | about 0 |

My estimate: on Slow 4G, first paint is 100–250 ms sooner on most routes. Main content is 60–350 ms sooner on /products, /categories and /community, and about 0 on /product and the category listings.

Best design:
- Do the motion fixes (all three entry imports split, as described in the reason).
- Leave Home eager; splitting it costs / about 120 ms.
- Skip the translation split (about 15 ms).

On a typical 4G link (about 10 Mbps), the 31 KB saves about 25 ms, plus about 15 ms of CPU: roughly 40 ms. Repeat visits gain nothing, because the vendor chunks are immutable and cached, and their hashes survive deploys.

Severity should be low-medium, not medium. Expect about half the stated gain.

confirmed.title: Community pages wait for the session answer before even asking whether the community is open
confirmed.cause: useCommunityAccess keys its request on the session (`const key = isLoaded ? user?.id ?? 'guest' : ''`) and returns early while the key is empty (access.tsx:107,121). So /api/community/access leaves only after /api/auth/me has answered. CommunityGate renders nothing (access.tsx:230-232) until then, and the server answers access from the cookie anyway.
confirmed.measured: /community phone trace: /api/auth/me 2210→2557 ms; /api/community/access requested only at 2589 → 3203 ms; LCP (the h1 «ليفو كوميونيتي تحت الصيانة») at 3288 ms. A/B with access preloaded in the document: LCP 3204 → 2888 ms (−0.32 s).
confirmed.fix: Prime /api/community/access in bootRequests (src/lib/bootFetch.ts:195) for community paths, or request it immediately with a 'pending' key and re-key once the session is known. Expected −0.3 to −0.45 s on every gated community page.
reasons:
I could not refute this. The finding is real, its cause is correct, and "low" is the right rating.

Code (perf/live 7c7190b, /home/user/levonis-perf):
- In src/pages/community/access.tsx, line 107 sets `const key = isLoaded ? user?.id ?? 'guest' : ''`. Line 121 returns early while the key is empty. CommunityGate then renders `fallback ?? null` at lines 230-232, and none of the gated routes in src/App.tsx (lines 949-986) passes a fallback.
- isLoaded only becomes true in the `.finally` of AuthContext's own `/api/auth/me` effect (src/AuthContext.tsx lines 53-66), and that request starts only after React has mounted.
- bootRequests in src/lib/bootFetch.ts (lines 195-215) primes only resolve, home and the product reads. Nothing primes or inlines `/api/community/access`: the live `/community` and `/requests` documents carry no lv-* data block and no preload.
- Nothing in docs/PERFORMANCE_LOG.md or docs/DECISIONS.md touches this chain, so it is not already fixed.
- The server answers per cookie. `/api/community/access` is edge-cached for guests (`public, max-age=60, s-maxage=120`, `Vary: Cookie`, cf HIT) and returned `{"closed":true,"may_enter":false}` live. So the client gains nothing by waiting for the session first, and the primed answer belongs to the same cookie that `/me` reads.

Live re-measurement: script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-communityaccess/ab.mjs, log ab.log in the same folder. Phone profile 360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, Slow-4G with 150 ms added latency, cold context for every visit. The priming was emulated at the exact moment bootFetch evaluates.
- /community, 6 runs per variant:
  - A (live): median LCP 3268 ms. The access request always leaves 30-60 ms after `/me` ends. The gap from the end of `/me` to the card was 293-654 ms (median about 320).
  - P (the proposed fix 1, prime access at boot, gate still waits for the session): median LCP 2754. The gap from the end of `/me` to the card falls to 35-189 ms.
  - Q (fix 2, the gate does not wait for `/me`): median LCP 2398.
- /requests, 4 runs: A 5228 → P 4806 → Q 4788. On this route the card also waits for the lazy Requests chunk that RunningCommunityOrders imports (App.tsx lines 77-78, 978). That chunk is requested only after the gate decides, so priming access moves that whole chain earlier.
- The earlier skeptic-authme-b run gives the same picture. With `/me` already primed, also priming access took LCP from 2804 to 2476 (−0.33 s), so this gain stays even if `/me` priming lands first.

Why "low" holds: it costs nothing on `/`, /products or the product pages. While the community is shut, BottomNav (lines 171-177) hides the community tab, so these routes are reached only through typed or shared links, the /requests flow or a store link.

Fix: option 1 is sound. Prime the access request in bootRequests for paths under /community, /u/ and /requests (also /followed-stores), and have accessFor take it with takePrimedJson so the session-epoch guard still applies. Option 2 removes the most: key the cache on the cookie rather than on user.id, so the gate shows without waiting for `/me`. Login and logout already clear primed requests. On a page where nothing else is late, this also takes `/me` itself (uncached, 0.3-1.0 s live) off the path to the card. Only the sign-in button inside the card would appear a little later.

The finding is real. I couldn't refute it, but its first proposed fix doesn't work on its own.

Code (live 7c7190b, unchanged since then; the live bundle /assets/index-oWU6EvxE.js still has `s=t?(e==null?void 0:e.id)??"guest":""`):
- src/pages/community/access.tsx:107 sets `key = isLoaded ? user?.id ?? 'guest' : ''`.
- access.tsx:121 returns early while the key is ''.
- isLoaded only turns true in the `.finally` of /api/auth/me (src/AuthContext.tsx:54-63).
- CommunityGate (access.tsx:230-232) renders `fallback ?? null`, and App.tsx:949-986 passes no fallback to /community, /community/projects/*, /u/:username, /community/store/*, /requests/*, /followed-stores or /community/saved.
- bootRequests (src/lib/bootFetch.ts:189-207) never starts /api/community/access.
- Nothing else handles this: the edge-cached guest answer (cf=HIT, `public, s-maxage=120, Vary: Cookie`) only shortens the hop; it doesn't remove it. The server answers per cookie (worker/lib/session.ts:61), so a request that leaves early would get the right answer for whoever holds the cookie.

Live evidence:
- In live-1.log, /community phone run 1 shows /api/auth/me from 2398 to 2863 ms. /api/community/access starts only at 2895 (32 ms after /me ends) and ends at 3126. LCP is 3192 on the card h1.
- In all 16 of my own "A" visits, the access request started 10 to 300 ms after /me finished.

My own A/B, run myself against the live site:
- Phone profile: 360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G with 150 ms RTT, cold, service worker blocked.
- The live index chunk was intercepted at the response stage in every variant, after it had crossed the throttled network, so only the patched variants change.
- n=5 interleaved runs per variant on /community. Medians:

| Variant | What it does | Gate shown (ms) | LCP (ms) | LCP change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | live code as is | 2884 | 2932 | — |
| P | access fetched at boot, gate still waits for /me (proposed fix 1) | 2871 | 3048 | none |
| K | hook keyed "guest" before /me answers, so it stops waiting for /me | 2649 | 2700 | −232 |
| PK | both P and K | 2512 | 2508 | −424 (gate −372) |

- A pooled sample with an earlier skeptic run on the same harness (11 A, 11 P) gives a gate median of 2961 → 2853 for P. That is only −110 ms.
- That run's /requests numbers also show the chain: A LCP 5228, P 4806, and a variant that removes /me from the network 4788.

Why fix 1 alone does nothing: the gate is still bounded by /me's latency, and that latency has a tail. Cookieless curl of /api/auth/me gave a TTFB of 137 to 165 ms typically, but 5 of 15 requests took 625 to 1104 ms. Several browser visits saw /me take about 1.0 s. Some of that tail may come from this sandbox's proxy, since an edge-cached /api/community/access also took 650 ms twice. Either way, fix 1 leaves the card waiting on it.

Rating: low is correct. It costs one edge round trip plus a re-render, and exposure to /me's tail, on every gated community page. Today the payload is only the maintenance card. Once the community opens, the same chain also delays every gated page's own data requests and images, so it would matter more.

Corrected fix:
1. Don't block the gate on the session. Start the request at once (the hook keyed "guest" before /me answers, as in the K test).
2. When /me answers, keep that same answer under user.id (or 'guest') instead of asking again. The server already answered for that cookie, so there is no maintenance-card flash for an allow-listed member.
3. Also prime /api/community/access in bootRequests for gated paths, and take it with takePrimedJson in fetchCommunityAccess.

Proposed fix 2 says "re-key once the session is known". If re-keying means a new request, it would set access back to null and the page would go blank again.

Request budget: about 330 browser requests over 22 visits, plus 20 curls. All anonymous reads. Scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-communityaccess-me/ (ab.mjs, ab.log).
gains: Phone, live A/B by median LCP. Fix 1 (prime access, keep waiting for the session) is the cleanest measure: about −0.3 s on /community. The gap from the end of /me to the card fell from about 320 ms to about 60 ms. The raw medians, 3268 → 2754 ms (−0.51 s), include noise from /me timing. On /requests, 5228 → 4806 ms (−0.42 s). Fix 2 (do not wait for /me at all): /community 3268 → 2398 ms (−0.87 s, because the uncached /me, 0.3-1.0 s live, also leaves the path to the card); /requests 4788 ms, no better than fix 1 because the lazy Requests chunk dominates there. Only the gated community, /u/ and /requests routes are affected, and they get little traffic while the community is shut.

Measured phone medians on /community (emulated Slow-4G, CPU ×4, n=5 per variant). Fix 1 alone (prime only): about 0 ms (gate 2884 → 2871, LCP 2932 → 3048), or −110 ms gate when pooled with the earlier run. Gate stops waiting for /me: LCP −232 ms (2932 → 2700). Both together: LCP −424 ms (2932 → 2508), gate −372 ms. On a real Iraqi 4G phone (about 60-120 ms to an edge-cached colo), I estimate 0.15 to 0.35 s for the combined fix on every gated community page. More if /me hits its tail (seen at 0.6 to 1.1 s), and more again once the community opens and the gated pages' own data and images queue behind this chain.

confirmed.title: The mascot's and the marquee's animation loops and forced layouts compete with the first render and the content render
confirmed.cause: Marquee measures in a useLayoutEffect (Marquee.tsx:151-185), reading clientWidth, getBoundingClientRect, scrollWidth and getComputedStyle. That forces a synchronous layout during the first commit, then setCopies triggers another render and layout before paint. Its requestAnimationFrame loop (Marquee.tsx:226/300) then reads scroll metrics every frame. AppIntro starts its own per-frame character loop (src/components/bloub/AppIntro.tsx, single rAF loop ~line 625) as soon as its chunk mounts. Both run while the page's data render and images are still being processed.
confirmed.measured:
CPU profile of cold / on a ×4 phone:
- First 9 s: AppIntro's rAF ~664 ms (pe 569, Ct 57, evaluation 38) and the marquee loop V 342 ms, against 974 ms of React rendering.
- First 4.2 s: marquee measure() has 191 ms self time (forced layout in commit); the LiveSearch layout effect 85 ms; scroll restore 39 ms.
- Main-thread trace: first-render task 407 ms (Layout 79) and data-render task 359 ms (Layout 97).
confirmed.fix:
- Start the marquee loop and the mascot's idle animation only after afterCriticalPaint, and pause them off-screen (IntersectionObserver).
- Size the marquee with CSS (or measure in a post-paint rAF) instead of setCopies in a layout effect.

Expected: about 0.1–0.2 s earlier first render on '/' and ~0.9 s less main-thread contention in the first 9 s on a ×4 phone.
reasons:
The cost is real but the finding puts it in the wrong place, rates it wrong and proposes a fix that misses it. I re-measured on live https://levonis-iq.com (index-oWU6EvxE.js; Marquee/AppIntro code unchanged since 7c7190b) with a 360×800 DPR3 phone, CPU ×4 and Slow-4G. For the A/B runs I patched the two bundles only inside my own browser (page.route). Every variant, base included, was served the same way. Scripts and results are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-loops/.

REFUTED PART: "competes with the first render / 0.1–0.2 s earlier first render on '/'".
- The marquee is never in the first commit. homeAds come from settings (Home.tsx:172, 264). Settings are fetched after mount (WalletContext.tsx:121). In 25 of 25 loads, .lv-mq__track was inserted 120–272 ms after FCP. So the useLayoutEffect measure (Marquee.tsx:173) and setCopies (copies went 3→4) cannot delay FCP.
- LCP on '/' is the h1, at the same moment as FCP.
- AppIntro mounts about 300 ms after FCP. Before FCP the rAF callbacks ran for 0–14 ms in total.
- FCP=LCP medians on '/' (n=5 each): base 2188, layout-effect→effect 2108, mascot loop off 2184, both off 2160. That is noise.
- /products LCP: 3380 vs 3244 with the mascot off. Category LCP: 5336 vs 5288. Home below-fold sections ready: 3695–3994 vs 3862–3923. All within noise.

REAL PART, and bigger than stated. The loops never stop. AppIntro's loop "always is [turning] while the tab is visible" (AppIntro.tsx:965-967). stop() runs only when the tab is hidden or on unmount (1016, 1093). While docked and idle, the mascot rewrites about 380–400 SVG attributes per second (path d values via BloubHome.tsx:72-115 from AppIntro.tsx:625/694). That repaints a gradient- and clip-filled SVG every frame. The marquee writes scrollLeft every frame (Marquee.tsx:226/296/300), even off-screen.
- Trace from FCP to 9 s on '/': main thread busy 5.1–5.6 s with base vs 1.0–1.4 s with both off.
  - Mascot alone ≈ 3.5 s: paint/prepaint/layerize/commit 1.5–1.9 s, style about 0.5 s, JS 0.6–0.8 s.
  - Marquee ≈ 1.9 s.
- The finding's 664 + 342 ms counts JS self time only, so it understates the cost about 3–4×.
- 10 s after load, a React-like job that yields every 5 ms gets this share of the main thread:
  - base: 0.34–0.44
  - both off: 0.97
  - '/' with only the marquee running: 0.76–0.79
  - /products with the mascot off: 0.97

WHERE IT COSTS DISPLAY TIME. Every client-side navigation renders inside startTransition (NavigationRouter.tsx:46-51). That render is time-sliced, so it runs at about 0.4× speed between loop frames.
- Back then forward '/'→'/products', grid painted: base median 702 ms (308–1117, n=7) vs both off 289 ms (185–355, n=7). Mascot off alone: 295 ms (n=3). Marquee off alone: 525 ms (n=3).
- Cold '/'→'/products' tap: base median 787 ms (642–1414) vs 657 ms (593–709, plus one 1680 outlier).
- Plain fetch-driven renders are not sliced, so first loads lose at most about one frame.

SEVERITY AND FIX.
- It is not a first-load cause. It is a medium-severity cause of slow page-to-page display on phones, and the mascot is the main part.
- "Start after afterCriticalPaint" changes nothing: both loops already start after FCP, and the cost is in steady state.
- The IntersectionObserver pause does not apply to the mascot, which is always on screen in the nav bar.
- Right fix:
  - Stop AppIntro's rAF loop when the character is docked with no journey, no blend and no attention change. Give the idle breathing and blink to a compositor animation (CSS/WAAPI transform/opacity on the wrapper) or a much lower rate. Re-arm the loop through schedule() on events.
  - Pause both loops while the navigation transition is pending.
  - Make the marquee a compositor transform animation, or pause it off-screen and during transitions.

The CPU cost is real, but on a phone it comes after the page is already on screen, so it does not slow display. I re-measured on live https://levonis-iq.com with the phone profile from scripts/perf-live-audit.mjs (360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G, cold) and re-read the code (live Marquee.tsx, AppIntro.tsx, Home.tsx and App.tsx are unchanged from 7c7190b to the current default-branch head).

1) Neither loop runs before the first paint. Both run only after the first paint, and the mascot's starts only after the data is painted. A/B with rAF wrapped and callbacks classified (scratchpad/perf/skeptic-loops-x/ab.mjs, ab.log, 8 interleaved rounds per variant):
- The marquee's first tick lands at 2661–3199 ms, after FCP (2460–2960) in 8/8 runs. Its first tick is in the frame that paints the data.
- The mascot's first tick lands at 2803–3381 ms, after the data paint (2700–3249) in 8/8 runs.
- The home LCP is the h1 text, and FCP = LCP.
- The ads Marquee mounts only once /api/home has returned settings.homeAds (Home.tsx:264). That is the data commit about 250 ms after FCP, not the first commit as the finding says. BrandMarquee (Strips.tsx:334) is not imported anywhere, so it never renders.
- AppIntro is React.lazy (App.tsx:493), and its loop starts in an effect once its chunk mounts (AppIntro.tsx:693-701).

2) Removing both loops entirely (variant B, the upper bound of the proposed fix) does not show anything sooner:
- '/' FCP/LCP median: A 2500 ms, B 2602 ms (noise, B was slower).
- Data paint after FCP: A 264 ms, B 248 ms.
- /api/home/sections request (afterCriticalPaint fires): A 4126 ms, B 4299 ms.
- Slowest route /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials, 6 rounds: LCP median A 5880 ms, B 5752 ms. That is within the spread of the runs (A 5372–6084 plus one 8084 outlier, B 5296–6200). TBT is the same (329 vs 361 ms).
- The CPU numbers do reproduce: in the first 9 s the mascot takes 478–683 ms and the marquee 316–391 ms at ×4. That is about 1.7 ms and about 1 ms per frame, all after display.

3) The marquee's "191 ms forced layout" is not extra work. Traces (trace.mjs and parse.py, with stack traces):
- measure() reading clientWidth (index-oWU6EvxE.js:126:67405) forces the data commit's own layout: 57–70 ms at ×4, 118 dirty of 221 objects.
- Variant C has the layout effect patched to useEffect. The same 118-of-221 layout still runs, at 77–94 ms. Total layout from 1.5 to 4.5 s is 184–243 ms in the unpatched traces and 216–288 ms in C, so there is no saving.
- The only extra cost of setCopies (3 → 4 copies, layout effect re-run) is a 3–5 ms partial relayout at ×4, about 1 ms on a real phone.

4) Pausing off-screen would not help at load. The ticker sits in the first screen right under the hero, and the mascot is always in view.

What is left is an ongoing main-thread cost after display, about 2.7 ms per frame at ×4. That matters for smoothness and battery, not for how fast pages appear. It turns some short tasks after the data paint into long tasks: on '/' the total long-task time is 847 vs 734 ms and TBT 597 vs 530 ms (A vs B). It deserves a separate smoothness/battery entry, not a slow-display one.
gains: First load: about 0 (≤0.1 s, within noise; FCP/LCP medians 2188 vs 2160 on '/', 3380 vs 3244 on /products, n=4–5). Client-side navigation on a ×4 Slow-4G phone: the next page paints about 0.1–0.4 s earlier at the median, and up to about 0.8 s earlier in the slow tail. Warm '/'→'/products' grid paint: 702 → 289 ms median (n=7 each); 295 ms with only the mascot loop removed. Cold tap: 787 → 657 ms. In steady state, about 3.5 s (mascot) + 1.9 s (marquee) of main thread per 6.5 s is freed at ×4. A 5 ms-sliced job's share of the main thread rises from 0.34–0.44 to 0.97. The mascot gives about 80% of the gain and the marquee about 20%.

Display on a phone: about 0 ms. These are upper bounds, from removing both loops entirely, measured live with CPU ×4 and Slow-4G:
- '/' FCP/LCP: no gain (median 2500 → 2602 ms, noise).
- '/' data paint: −16 ms (noise).
- afterCriticalPaint / sections request: no gain (4126 → 4299 ms).
- Category listing LCP: −128 ms median, inside the run-to-run spread of the runs.
- Moving the marquee measure out of the layout effect: about 1 ms. The 57–70 ms layout it forces is the data commit's own layout, and it still runs at 77–94 ms when the measure is moved to useEffect.
Off the display path, the real saving is about 0.85–1.0 s of main-thread time in the first 9 s at ×4 (mascot 478–683 ms, marquee 316–391 ms), all after the data paint. On '/' that is about 70 ms less TBT and about 110 ms less long-task time: better input response and battery, not faster display. The finding's expected "0.1–0.2 s earlier first render on '/'" does not happen, because neither loop starts before the first paint.

confirmed.title: Category listing pages load as a 5-step serial waterfall: resolve, then route chunks, then catalog tree, then products, then images
confirmed.cause: `assetWithPreview` only rewrites the main-host opening documents for '/' and '/products' (worker/index.ts:878 `mainOpening`). Category documents leave as the plain asset, with no inline resolve answer, no modulepreload of the route chunk graph and no API preload. In the browser, src/App.tsx:706 (`if (!resolved) return <RouteFallback />`) holds every route until GET /api/storefront/resolve returns, so the lazy CategoryListing chunk and its 24 dependencies are requested only after that round trip. Then src/pages/CategoryListing.tsx:51-58 starts loadTree() and line 98 (`if (!tree ...) return <ListingSkeleton />`) keeps ListingView unmounted until the tree arrives. Only then is /api/products?category=<id>&facets=1&limit=24 requested, because the id comes from the tree, and only after that do the card images start.
confirmed.measured: Live audit, phone medians: fdm-materials LCP 5992 ms, printer-accessories 5980 ms, /products 3304 ms. Live fdm run: resolve starts 2067 ms (299 ms), tree starts 4047 ms, products start 4495 ms and take 766 ms (MISS), LCP 5992 ms. My cold phone trace (runs/fdm.json): document 0–358, entry JS until 1959, resolve 2103→3197, 24 route chunks 3221→4604, /api/catalog/tree 4656→5205, products 5398→6630 (20 KB), first card images 6792, LCP 7296 ms. Desktop: LCP 2760 ms.
confirmed.fix:
Treat /categories/* like /products in assetWithPreview:
- Inline the main-host resolve answer (it needs no DB read).
- Modulepreload the CategoryListing / CategoryPage chunk graph from the manifest (chunkPreloads).
- Preload /api/catalog/tree. Also preload the listing call, resolving slug to catalog id in the Worker from the memoised catalogIndexFor, or let the listing API accept the slug path.
- In CategoryListing, mount ListingView by slug without waiting for the tree.

Expected: the resolve round trip and the tree-then-products serialisation disappear, and the chunks, tree and products download in parallel from the document. Estimate: phone LCP about 6.0 s down to about 3.5 s, in line with /products, which already has these preloads.
reasons:
The finding is real. The size of the gain is overstated, and the proposed fix leaves out the step that makes it work.

CONFIRMED IN CODE (7c7190b):
- worker/index.ts:878: `mainOpening` only covers '/' and '/products'.
- src/App.tsx:706 holds every route on `if (!resolved) return <RouteFallback />`.
- src/pages/CategoryListing.tsx:51-58 calls loadTree(), and :98 shows `<ListingSkeleton />` until the tree arrives. The listing call needs `node.id` from the tree (:129-130).

CONFIRMED LIVE (curl):
- /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials and /categories/printer-accessories are served as the plain 5,327 B index.html. They have 3 modulepreloads (vendor only), no lv-resolve block and no preload-as-fetch.
- /products is 6,491 B, with lv-resolve, 12 route modulepreloads and a preload of /api/products?limit=50.

MY OWN A/B (scratchpad/perf/skeptic-catwaterfall/ab.mjs and run.log):
- Setup: the perf-live-audit phone profile (360x800, DPR 3, CPU x4, 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps), a cold context, no page.route, so the document arrives over the throttled network.
- The "fix" variant adds to <head>, as soon as it exists, what the proposed Worker change would write: the lv-resolve block, modulepreloads of the route closure (capped at 24, the chunkPreloads default), the closure CSS, and preload-as-fetch of the first read and the listing read. Request counts show each preload was consumed (one listing request and one catalog request per load).
- Base fdm: entry JS 287-1775; resolve 1951-2181 (in another run 2049-3257); route chunk starts only at 2226-3286; tree 3826-4090; listing 4327-4647 (it waits about 0.5 s on the tree); LCP image 4881-5427. LCP was 5476 and 6440.
- Fix fdm: resolve is inline; route chunk 314-1899; tree 303-1500; listing 303-2051. LCP was 4536 and 4656.
- printer-accessories: base 5688, fix 4640.
- An earlier, independent 3-run series (skeptic-headstart) agrees: fdm 5476 to 4224, pacc 5470 to 4294.

WHAT THE FINDING GETS WRONG:
1. The estimate of "about 6.0 s down to about 3.5 s, in line with /products" is too optimistic. Even with every preload in place, about 290 KB of JS (entry plus the 26-chunk CategoryListing / 28-chunk CategoryPage closure, against 12 chunks for Products) finishes downloading only at 3.6-3.85 s on Slow-4G. Content then paints at 3.7-3.95 s and LCP lands at about 4.5-4.65 s. The remaining roughly 1.2 s gap to /products comes from the heavier route chunk graph and from card images that start only after render. Those are separate causes.
2. The fix as written would do nothing. `/categories/*` is not in `run_worker_first`: not in env.staging (wrangler.jsonc:269-300), which serves levonis-iq.com, and not in the top-level block at :101. The asset layer answers those documents before the Worker exists. The live headers show this: `cache-control: no-cache` with a strong ETag, where /products gets the Worker's `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=60` with a weak ETag. So `/categories` and `/categories/*` must be added to all three run_worker_first lists, as well as to assetWithPreview.
3. For /categories/:cat (CategoryPage, src/pages/CategoryPage.tsx:78), the first read is /api/catalog/<slug>, not the tree. It can be preloaded straight from the URL slug, with no lookup.
4. chunkPreloads caps at 24, which is fewer than the 26 and 28 chunks in these closures. A small loss.

It is still one of the largest single causes on category pages, about 20% of phone LCP.

The waterfall is real and nothing else covers it. It is rated correctly as high. The estimate is too optimistic, and part of the proposed fix is wrong for /categories/:cat.

What is live, checked by curl just now:
- /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials and /categories/printer-accessories are served as the plain 5,327 B asset (cache-control: no-cache). They carry no lv-resolve block, no route modulepreload and no API preload.
- /products is 6,491 B and has the inline resolve answer, 12 route modulepreloads and a preload of /api/products?limit=50.

The code matches the finding:
- worker/index.ts:878: `mainOpening` covers only '/' and '/products'. The /categories paths never reach a rewrite branch, because `routeModuleFor` (worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:660) returns null for them.
- src/App.tsx:706 holds every route on `if (!resolved) return <RouteFallback />`.
- src/pages/CategoryListing.tsx:51-58 then 98 gates ListingView on loadTree().
- /categories/:cat is a different component, CategoryPage (src/App.tsx:1003). It gates on `loadCategory(slug)` at src/pages/CategoryPage.tsx:78 and line 124. It reads /api/catalog/<slug>, not the tree.
- No srcset, edge rule or later preload removes any of these steps.

My own live phone A/B (360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps, cold). The document is rewritten only inside the browser. Every arm gets the same 300 ms document delay.

fdm-materials:
- Base: LCP 6932 and 5524 ms (median 6228).
  - Resolve: 2170→3027 and 2079→2346.
  - Route chunks (26): start only after resolve, 3111→4752 and 2379→3967.
  - Tree: 4795 and 4027.
  - Listing: 5438 and 4419.
  - First image: 6420 and 4889.
- RMD, a Worker-only change (inline resolve, chunkPreloads with cap 24, preload /api/catalog/tree): LCP 4672 and 4668.
  - Chunks: 344→3199.
  - Tree: 344→1547.
  - Listing: 3467.
- RMDL, adding a preload of /api/products?category=cat_materials_fdm&facets=1&limit=24: LCP 4424 and 4608 (median 4516).

printer-accessories:
- Base: LCP 6424 and 6124 (median 6274).
- RMD, with /api/catalog/printer-accessories as the data preload: LCP 4784 and 4968 (median 4876).

FCP does not change (about 2.5–2.7 s).

Where the finding is wrong:
1. Phone LCP does not reach about 3.5 s. Once the gates are gone, the new critical path is the route closure: 26 chunks for CategoryListing and 28 for CategoryPage, against 12 for Products. Both exceed the cap of 24. On Slow-4G the closure finishes at about 3.2–3.6 s, so LCP settles at about 4.5–4.9 s.
2. The listing preload, which needs slug-to-id in the Worker, saves only about 150 ms. Mounting ListingView by slug on the client is not needed, because the preloaded tree arrives at about 1.5 s, long before the chunks.
3. Preloading /api/catalog/tree is the wrong data preload for /categories/:cat. CategoryPage needs /api/catalog/<slug>.

Run logs (live requests used: 369 + 216):
- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-catwaterfall-z/run-fdm.log
- /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-catwaterfall-z/run-pacc.log
gains: Phone (Slow-4G, CPU x4, cold): fdm-materials LCP went from about 5.96 s (median of 5476 and 6440) to about 4.60 s (4536 and 4656), saving about 1.0-1.9 s (median about 1.35 s). printer-accessories went from 5688 to 4640 ms, saving about 1.05 s. The earlier independent 3-run series measured about 1.2 s. LCP after the fix is about 4.5 s, not the claimed 3.5 s, because the 287-293 KB of route and entry JS still ends at about 3.7 s. Desktop gain is small and was not measured (desktop LCP is 2.76 s, with short round trips). I used about 360 live requests.

Phone LCP drops about 1.4–1.6 s, not the 2.5 s the finding claims.

- fdm-materials: 6228 → 4670 ms with the Worker-only change (resolve + modulepreload + tree preload), and → 4516 ms if the listing preload is added (n=2 each).
- printer-accessories: 6274 → 4876 ms with resolve + modulepreload + preload of /api/catalog/printer-accessories (n=2).

Cards appear about 1.4–1.7 s earlier: fdm 5671 → 3990 ms, accessories 5850 → 4464 ms. FCP stays the same.

Most of the gain comes from the cheap Worker change: extend mainOpening to /categories/* with chunkPreloads for CategoryListing or CategoryPage and the matching data preload. The listing preload adds about 150 ms, and the client change adds about 0.

The remaining gap to /products (about 3.3 s) is the 26–28 chunk route closure, which finishes around 3.2–3.6 s on Slow-4G. Desktop gain should be smaller (about 0.5 s or less, from 2.76 s); I did not measure it.

confirmed.title: The product's main photo is not preloaded on 25 of 26 live product pages, so it waits for all product JS and the first render
confirmed.cause: previewFrom() emits `preloadImage` only when `(!lightImage || lightImage === image)` and the selection cannot change the image (socialPreview.ts:414-420). 25 of the 26 live products have a light_image different from the primary, and 24 have option- or colour-bound media, so preloadImage is null. worker/index.ts:957-971 then writes no ``. The page's opening image is deterministic, though. A single public option is auto-selected (Product.tsx ~1247: `opts.length === 1`), which moves esun-pla-plus to its option photo. On the light theme ('system' is the default and phones are usually light), the primary's slot shows light_image (Product.tsx:2229-2233). Without a preload, the is created only after ~362 KB / 32 JS requests, the detail JSON and the Product render long task. In the h2d trace the image request went out 280 ms after FCP.
confirmed.measured:
I fetched all 26 live product documents: only 1 contains as="image". Live audit phone esun-pla-plus: FCP 3468 ms, LCP 4284 ms (816 ms gap). The one product with a preload (x2d) shows LCP − FCP = 184 ms in my trace, with the image request at 272 ms.

A/B on the live site (ab.mjs; same document served through page.route, arm B adds one preload for the image the page actually opens; phone throttled; median of 3):
- esun-pla-plus: image request start 3335 → 47 ms; LCP 4016 → 3296 ms (−720 ms); FCP unchanged.
- bambu-lab-pla-basic-filament (light image): image start 3664 → 81 ms; LCP 4364 → 3848 ms (−516 ms).
confirmed.fix:
Compute the opening image in the Worker with the page's own rule: initial_selection, otherwise a single option or colour, then productGalleryForSelection, otherwise the primary. Then do one of these:
- Emit two preloads, `media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"` for the light_image and `media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"` for the primary, each with its imagesrcset/imagesizes.
- Or have the theme boot script, which already resolves the theme before paint, add the one matching link. Its CSP hash lives in worker/lib/securityPolicy.ts.

Expected: −0.5 to −0.7 s phone LCP on 25/26 product pages (measured above).
reasons: The finding is real. My numbers are close to the audit's, but the gain depends on how big the lead image is, and parts of the proposed fix need correcting. What I checked in the code (/home/user/levonis-perf, 7c7190b): - worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:414-420 sets preloadImage to null whenever the product has a light_image different from the primary, or option/colour-bound media. - worker/index.ts:957-971 then writes no `as=image` preload. - Product.tsx:1249 opens a single public option automatically. - Product.tsx:2229-2233 shows light_image in the primary's slot on the light theme. It also sets width/height to null there, so the page's srcset is the full 160–1600 ladder with the default sizes. - No srcset, edge rule or service-worker path covers this: public/sw.js keeps /files network-only (PERFORMANCE_LOG P1a). What I checked live (my own curl, 2026-10-16): - Only 1 of the 26 product documents contains `as="image"` (bambu-lab-x2d-combo-open-box-workshop-2026). - I recomputed each page's opening image from /api/products/ using the page's own rule: - 21 products open on a theme-dependent lead (primary in dark, light_image in light). - 3 open on an option-bound image that is the same in both themes: esun-pla-plus (option photo fa41c4…, 1000×444), bambu-reusable-spool and levo-switch-blue-3pin. - x2d is already preloaded. - 0 of 26 currently have initial_selection set. My A/B: real browser, phone 360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, Slow-4G (150 ms latency, 1.6 Mbps). Same live document in every arm, delayed 600 ms; median of 3 pairs. - esun-pla-plus, one preload built from the repo's own variantSrcSet/productGallerySizes: LCP 4500 → 4124 ms (−376). The three pairs were −376, +308 and −704. In the +308 pair the lead (18.8 KB) was downloaded twice; I could not find why. - bambu-lab-pla-basic-filament on the light theme, with the proposed `media` pair (light_image preload with width null, primary preload with its 1254 width): LCP 5168 → 4296 ms (−872). The pairs were −1536, −352 and −872. The dark preload was never fetched, and the lead was not downloaded twice. - FCP did not change beyond noise (+90 / +136 ms in the medians). The Product JS finished at the same time (~2.6 s) in both arms. Why the gain has a ceiling: - The preload starts at ~650 ms. On a throttled link it competes with ~360 KB of JS, so it finishes only at 3.85–4.15 s. - The `` is inserted at 4.0–4.2 s in every arm. LCP can never come before that, so the gain is only the lead's own fetch after insertion: 0.36–0.85 s in arm A. - The image is inserted ~1.4 s after both the Product JS (~2.6 s) and the detail JSON (~2.1 s) have arrived. That render path is a larger cost, and this fix does not touch it. Where the finding is mis-rated or mis-scoped: 1. The gain grows with the lead's size. It is about −0.4 s for a small lead like esun (19 KB) and about −0.9 s for the 40–70 KB light leads. The claimed −0.5 to −0.7 s is roughly the middle, not a floor. 2. It helps only when the product page is the first document loaded (a shared link, a search result, a refresh). Opening a product from /products inside the app loads no new document, so it gets nothing. 3. The proposed step "initial_selection first" needs an inventory read on the document path. initial_selection is computed by firstUsableDirectSelection with inventory, at worker/routes/products.ts:4058. Today all 26 are null, but once stock exists the Worker would preload the wrong image unless it reads inventory or skips the preload for products with direct-sale stock. 4. The `media` pair preloads the wrong image when a visitor's saved theme (localStorage levonis.theme.v1) differs from the phone's setting. That wastes 20–70 KB and gains nothing. 5. The boot-script variant can handle a saved theme exactly. But the theme script sits at line 27 of the live head, before the stylesheet (line 44) and before the links the Worker injects just above ``. The Worker would therefore have to place the two URLs before the script, for example in a meta tag. The script's CSP hash is pinned in worker/lib/securityPolicy.ts:107-111. 6. The 3 option-led products need a single preload with no `media` condition. The light preload must be built with width null, as Product.tsx:2233 does, or it becomes a second download. Scratch evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-leadpreload/: esun-ab.log, bbf-ab.log, lead.cjs, scripts/ab.mjs, docs/ and api/.

The finding holds. The main photo really is discovered late, and a preload of the photo the page actually opens on takes 0.34 to 0.70 s off phone LCP without moving FCP. The rating is about right, but the expected gain is a little high for option-photo products, and the fix has two caveats. **Code (re-read on 7c7190b):** - `worker/lib/socialPreview.ts:414-420` sets `preloadImage` to null whenever `light_image` differs from the primary or a bound option/colour image exists. - `worker/index.ts:957-971` then writes no image preload. The document still preloads the detail JSON and 27 JS modules. - The suppression was a deliberate earlier fix (`docs/PERFORMANCE_LOG.md:1492-1505`): the A1 page had preloaded the wrong relation image, so preloading was switched off for those products. This finding refines that fix; it does not repeat it. - Nothing else covers the gap. There is no lazy wrapper or later srcset, and the service worker does not help a first visit. **Live re-measurement (my own):** - I fetched all 26 product documents. Only `bambu-lab-x2d-combo-open-box-workshop-2026` contains `as="image"`. - I loaded 4 products in Chromium in light and dark. The lead `` is the LCP element in every case, and the opening photo is fixed for each theme: - esun-pla-plus opens on its single option's photo in both themes (`Product.tsx:1250` auto-selects it). - basic-filament, h2d and key-ring open on `light_image` at `?w=1080` in light. The light file has no stored size, so `Product.tsx:2233` gives it the uncapped `sizes`. - In dark they open on the primary at `?w=800` (capped `sizes`). **My A/B on the live site:** Phone 360×800 DPR 3, CPU ×4, 1.6 Mbps / 150 ms. The document was swapped through raw CDP Fetch with the HTTP cache left on, as on a phone. Medians of 5–7 runs, LCP in ms: | Product (scheme) | As served | + one preload | + two media-gated preloads | FCP | |---|---|---|---|---| | esun-pla-plus (light) | 4316 | 3980 (−336) | — | 3452 → 3468 | | bambu-lab-pla-basic-filament (light) | 4628 | 3956 (−672) | 3928 (−700) | 3348 → 3280 | | bambu-lab-h2d (light) | 4284 | 3724 (−560) | 3660 (−624) | 3340 → 3356 | | bambu-lab-pla-basic-filament (dark) | 4280 | — | 3828 (−452) | 3344 → 3148 | - Without a preload, the image request goes out about 300 ms after FCP. With one, the gap between FCP and LCP shrinks from about 0.7–1.4 s to about 0.3–0.7 s. - The media link that does not match the visitor's scheme was never fetched, and no run downloaded the image twice. **Harness warning:** My first batch used Playwright `page.route`, as the finding's `ab.mjs` does. That turns off the HTTP cache, and it intermittently caused the preloaded image to be downloaded a second time, in both one-preload and two-preload arms. Under it, esun showed only −24 ms and the two-preload arm looked worse than no preload. The cache-on numbers above are the reliable ones; the finding's −720 ms for esun is high. **Caveats on the proposed fix:** 1. All 26 products are catalogue-only today (`source` is `catalog`, `price_status` is `unpriced`), so `initial_selection` is always null (`worker/routes/products.ts:3994-4021`). The shareable document deliberately does no stock read (`socialPreview.ts:395-396`). Each preload has to mirror its `` exactly: the uncapped `sizes` for `light_image` (it has no width or height) and the stored aspect for the primary or option photo. Otherwise it becomes a second download. 3. The two media-gated preloads pick the wrong image for a visitor who saved a theme opposite to their device's. That costs one extra 27–55 KB image and no gain for them. The theme boot script variant avoids this, but its CSP hash in `worker/lib/securityPolicy.ts:107-111` must change with it. Logs and scripts are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-leadpreload-q/` (`ab3-*.log`, `bin/ab3.mjs`, `bin/opening.mjs`).

About −0.34 to −0.70 s phone LCP on 25 of 26 product pages, with FCP unchanged. Measured as cache-on median LCP on the live site against the current document:
