confirmed.title: Edge cache for the listing and product APIs is never served stale; every first visitor after 120 s pays a full D1 rebuild of 0.6–1.3 s
confirmed.cause: anonymousCached() stores answers in caches.default with `s-maxage=120, stale-while-revalidate=600` (ANONYMOUS_LIFETIME, edgePolicy.ts:89) and reads them with `cache.match(key)` (line 218). The Workers Cache API does not implement stale-while-revalidate: an entry past 120 s is simply gone, and the request rebuilds the whole answer from D1 inline. The file's own comment assumes "ten more minutes in which a colo may answer stale", which does not happen. On a low-traffic shop most real visits arrive after the 2-minute window, so they pay the miss.
confirmed.measured:
curl, anonymous GETs:
- /api/products?limit=41|42|43 (fresh keys): MISS server TTFB 0.62 / 0.76 / 0.98 s; immediate repeat HIT 0.06–0.08 s.
- Same keys at age 103 s: still HIT.
- Same keys at about 156 s and again at about 7 min: no cf-cache-status (MISS), TTFB 0.58–1.32 s.
- /api/products/esun-pla-plus, after earlier HITs: MISS 1.03 s at 07:53.
- Live audit phone /products: /api/products?limit=50 cf MISS, 1998 ms, versus desktop HIT 446 ms.
- My /products phone trace: API headers at 4094 ms, after all JS (3804 ms), so the miss decided when cards could render.
- Live fdm listing API: MISS, 766 ms, inside the serial chain.
confirmed.fix:
Implement stale-while-revalidate in anonymousCached:
- Put entries with a long edge TTL (e.g. s-maxage 3600) plus an internal fresh-until header.
- On a hit past fresh-until, return the stored body immediately and rebuild in c.executionCtx.waitUntil, guarded by a per-key in-flight flag.
- The existing purge seams (purgeAnonymousCache on admin writes) keep correctness.

Expected: the first visitor per colo per 2 min gets a 60–80 ms answer instead of 0.6–1.3 s. That moves /products and category LCP by up to that amount whenever the entry has aged out.
reasons:
The cause is real, but the finding overstates the cost, wrongly includes the product page, and the proposed fix as written would break price freshness.

CODE (head 7c7190b). worker/lib/edgePolicy.ts:89 sets ANONYMOUS_LIFETIME to s-maxage 120 and stale-while-revalidate 600. Line 218 reads with a plain `cache.match(key)`, and line 233 writes with `cache.put`. Nothing serves an entry once it has expired. There is no fresh-until header, no stale branch and no background rebuild anywhere in the code, and no later commit added any. The header comment at lines 27-31 assumes "ten more minutes in which a colo may answer stale", and the Workers Cache API does not do that.

LIVE CONFIRMATION (IAD colo, curl). Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-edgeswr-v/expiry.log
- Two fresh keys, `/api/products?limit=17` and the fdm listing with limit=19.
- At t=0 both missed (TTFB 1592 and 649 ms). They were then HITs at ages 2, 58, 108 and 115 s (TTFB 64-153 ms).
- At t=424 both missed (TTFB 756 and 979 ms; one repeat took 3248 ms). An age of about 422 s is well inside the 600 s stale window the header advertises, so nothing is ever served stale.

DISPLAY COST ON A PHONE. Controlled A/B with the audit's phone profile (360x800, DPR 3, CPU x4, 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps).
- Method: the page's own listing request is rewritten in the browser's throttled network stack to an equivalent key. A never-used `limit` forces a MISS; a key stored a few seconds earlier gives a HIT. On these pages total is smaller than limit, so the body is the same. Each visit is classified by the cf-cache-status it actually got.
- Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-edgeswr-v/ab.log
- /products, 4 HIT vs 4 MISS:
  - API TTFB median 85 vs 809 ms.
  - First card in the DOM 3243 vs 3675 ms (+432 ms).
  - LCP 3686 vs 4130 ms (+444 ms).
  - The document preloads the API at about 300 ms, but the request is only sent at 1.5-2.5 s. A HIT finishes at 2.1-2.4 s, before the JS (about 3.0 s). A MISS finishes at 3.1-3.7 s, so the cards wait for it.
  - The cost scales with the miss. A 564 ms miss cost about 0 ms; a 1461 ms miss cost about 700 ms.
- /categories/printing-materials/fdm-materials, 2 HIT vs 6 MISS (two HIT arms also came back as misses):
  - Here the listing is not preloaded and sits at the end of a serial chain, starting at 5.1-6.7 s.
  - API TTFB median 204 vs 713 ms.
  - Time from listing start to first card 708 vs 1230 ms (+520 ms), added straight onto the cards.
- /product/:slug, the finding is wrong here. Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-edgeswr-v/detail.log
  - Four slugs, with the document warmed by curl first. Each got a cold-API visit, then a warm one.
  - The detail API is preloaded by the document (worker/index.ts:967). Even on a MISS (TTFB 268-1159 ms) it finishes at 1.8-3.0 s, while the JS finishes at 3.8-5.1 s.
  - Product title in the DOM: median about 4003 vs 3883 ms, within noise. LCP medians are about 4600 vs 4636 ms, so no difference.
  - The detail miss costs nothing on the screen.

MIS-RATED.
- A HIT still runs the Worker, so it answers in 53-302 ms, not 60-80 ms.
- On /products part of the miss overlaps the JS download, so a miss costs about 0.4-0.5 s of display time, not 0.6-1.3 s.
- The product page should be dropped from the finding.
- What the finding leaves out: the same helper also serves `/api/storefront/resolve`, `/api/community/access` and `/api/settings/public`. On an aged category visit all of them miss together. One fix in `anonymousCached` therefore helps the whole category chain.

MIS-FIXED.
- The proposal stores entries for 3600 s and says "the existing purge seams keep correctness". That is false for exactly the keys in question.
- `purgeAnonymousCache` (edgePolicy.ts:240-252) deletes only the parameter-less key. `cataloguePaths` names only '/api/products' (line 333).
- So `/api/products?limit=50` and every `?category=…&facets=1&limit=24` key are never purged. Today they are bounded only by the 120 s expiry.
- With a 3600 s stored lifetime, the first visitor in each colo could be shown prices or stock up to an hour old after an admin change.
- The safe version: store for at most 120+600 = 720 s, the window the header and the comment on `CATALOG_CACHE_EPOCH` in worker/lib/publicApi/cache.ts already promise.
  - Serve stale between 120 and 720 s.
  - Rebuild in `waitUntil` with a per-isolate in-flight guard.
  - Re-stamp the projection header and ETag.
- The alternative is a catalogue-generation stamp in the key, so writes invalidate the parameterised keys.
- With the 720 s cap, the fix only helps a visit that arrives 120-720 s after the last refresh of that same key in that colo. A visit after a longer quiet gap still pays the full miss. So the gain is real but intermittent on a low-traffic shop.

The mechanism is real, but the finding overstates the cost. It is right for listing and category pages and wrong for the product page.

CONFIRMED (re-measured from IAD with my own fresh key):
- anonymousCached stores with s-maxage=120 (worker/lib/edgePolicy.ts:89) and reads with a plain cache.match (:218). Nothing serves stale.
- Fresh key /api/products?limit=19:
  - t=1: MISS, 1029 ms server
  - t=107: HIT, age 106, 89 ms
  - t=126: HIT, age 118, 132 ms
  - t=136: MISS, 2424 ms
- That last MISS falls inside the "stale-while-revalidate=600" window the header promises, so the 600 s is never used. The file comment's "a colo may answer stale" (edgePolicy.ts header comment) does not happen.
- The shop has 27 products and low traffic, so most first page views in a colo come after an entry has aged out.
- Nothing else hides it:
  - Products.tsx:105 and Product.tsx:1156 only take the primed request; the browser keeps no copy between visits (bootFetch.ts: "nothing here caches an answer").
  - A cron warmer could not help, because the Cache API is per colo.

MIS-RATED FOR /product/:slug (my phone A/B: 360×800 DPR3, CPU×4, Slow-4G, cold browser each visit; MISS visit, then HIT visit straight after):
- The product document preloads the detail JSON (worker/index.ts:967, `<link rel=preload as=fetch>`).
- On a MISS the JSON (440–1304 ms server) finished at 2.0–3.1 s. The last JS finished at 4.0–4.3 s. The page shows its skeleton until both are in (Product.tsx:2143).
- Results, MISS vs HIT:

| Product | Title appears (h1) | LCP |
|---|---|---|
| galaxy | 3888 vs 3860 | 4696 vs 4712 |
| spool | 3945 vs 3759 | 4648 vs 4264 |
| marble | 4566 vs 3899 | 5784 vs 4680 |

- The marble pair is noise: its FCP also moved by 572 ms, and FCP is painted before the JSON matters.
- So on the product page the miss is hidden behind the JS: about 0 ms.

/products, PARTLY HIDDEN:
- The document preloads /api/products?limit=50 (index.ts:888), so it overlaps the JS download.
- In the earlier natural cold/warm runs (perf/skeptic-swr/ab.log), a MISS of about 0.5 s cost about +110 ms of LCP (3576 vs 3464, 3532 vs 3416).
- In the live audit the phone MISS took 1998 ms from 311 ms, with LCP 3304. In runs where the URL was rewritten to force a miss (perf/skeptic-edgeswr-v) the cost was about +0.4 s.
- A HIT is not 60 ms on a phone: it is about 200–450 ms with Slow-4G latency and transfer.

CATEGORY PAGES, REAL AND WORST:
- The listing leaves last in a serial chain, at 4.5–4.9 s on the phone (live-1.log). Every millisecond of the miss lands on LCP.
- Live: fdm listing MISS 766 ms on the phone vs HIT 199 ms on desktop.
- With the whole chain cold vs warm (natural runs), category LCP rose 0.57–1.1 s (6260/5152, 6024/5252, 5516/4948).

FIX NEEDS CORRECTION:
1. A put lifetime of 3600 s raises the worst-case staleness from the documented 12 min to about 62 min. Purges are per colo (purgeAnonymousCache), so other colos would serve prices and stock up to an hour old. Use sMaxAge + staleWhileRevalidate (720 s), which keeps the bound the owner already accepted, unless the owner decides otherwise.
2. /api/catalog/* has its own Cache API path with s-maxage=300 and no stale serving (worker/routes/catalog.ts:58). It sits in the same category chain, so it needs the same treatment or the category gain is only partly realised.
3. The in-flight flag only works within one isolate. That is acceptable, but it is no guarantee of a single rebuild.
4. Cloudflare may evict rarely-read Cache API entries before their TTL, so a long TTL does not guarantee hits in a low-traffic Iraqi colo.

Severity: high for category pages, medium for /products, none for product pages.
gains:
Per affected visit, on a phone (measured from the IAD colo):
- /products: about 0.43 s sooner on cards and LCP (median 4 MISS vs 4 HIT; range 0 to about 0.7 s, growing with the miss).
- Category pages: about 0.5 s sooner on cards per listing request. A bit more when resolve, community/access and settings/public would also have missed in the same chain (skeptic-swr/ab.log saw those miss together).
- /product/:slug: about 0 (the API is preloaded and finishes 1-2 s before the JS; LCP medians 4600 vs 4636 ms).

How often it applies, with the safe 720 s cap: only visits arriving 120-720 s after the last refresh of that key in that colo. Weighted by that, the expected gain is probably 0.1-0.3 s on average for listing pages, and still 0.4-0.5 s whenever it triggers.

Iraqi colos could not be measured. Their D1 distance and their split of traffic across several colos may shift both numbers.

These are gains on a phone (Slow-4G, CPU×4, DPR3) when the colo's entry has aged out, which on this low-traffic site is most first visits.

| Page | Gain from stale serving | How it was measured |
|---|---|---|
| /product/:slug | about 0 ms | My A/B: the MISS JSON finished 1.2–1.9 s before the last JS; h1 moved +28 and +186 ms and LCP −16 and +384 ms in the two clean pairs, both within noise |
| /products | about 0.1–0.4 s LCP | Natural cold/warm runs: +110 ms when the MISS took about 0.5 s; more when it took 1–2 s, as in the live audit (1998 ms) |
| /categories/:cat/:sub, listing only | about 0.4–0.6 s LCP | Live: MISS 766 ms vs a phone HIT of about 200–300 ms, at the end of the serial chain |
| /categories/:cat/:sub, whole chain | about 0.6–1.1 s LCP | Natural cold vs warm runs: 6260/5152, 6024/5252, 5516/4948 |

The whole-chain figure is reached only if catalog.ts's separate cache also gets stale serving.

The finding's "0.6–1.3 s on every first visit" overstates it: a phone HIT costs about 200–450 ms, not 60–80 ms. It is roughly right only for the serial category chain.

confirmed.title: The product route shows a blank screen until ~130 KB of route JS in 23 chunks arrives; vendor-motion is pulled in by Note.tsx
confirmed.cause:
The Product route's Suspense fallback is `<RouteFallback productHeader>` (App.tsx:113-139, 905): a black min-h-dvh div with only the mascot header, so nothing contentful paints until the Product chunk graph is downloaded, parsed and rendered. ProductDetailSkeleton, which lives in the entry's ui/Skeleton, is shown only after the chunk has arrived (Product.tsx:2143-2160).

The graph is the Product chunk (40.8 KB br / 131.8 KB raw) plus 22 static dependencies. Two of those dependencies are avoidable on the critical path:
- src/components/ui/Note.tsx:21 `import { motion } from 'motion/react'` uses the full proxy, which drags vendor-motion (16.9 KB br / 52.6 KB raw, the motion features the home deliberately defers) into the product's first render.
- vendor-icons (13.7 KB br / 71 KB raw) holds every icon shared by two or more lazy modules.
confirmed.measured:
Live audit phone FCP medians: /product/esun-pla-plus 3468 ms; /products 2320; / 2476; /categories 2292 (about +1.1 s on product pages).

Trace runs/esun1.json: 32 scripts, 362 KB. Product-only chunks: 23 requests, 130.4 KB. vendor-motion was the last script to finish (1394 → 4228 ms). FCP 4436 ms in that run (3208 ms in runs/esun-pla-plus-b).

Manifest closure from the live /.vite/manifest.json: `_Note-DmbYupEC.js` is the only Product dependency that imports `_vendor-motion-DDNunUBr.js`. Product-DDcst-Cj.js was cf=MISS (2079 ms) in the live phone run.
confirmed.fix:
1) Use ProductDetailSkeleton (already in the entry) as the product route's Suspense fallback, so the first contentful paint happens when the entry has executed (about 2.3 s, as on /products), not after the product graph.
2) Switch Note.tsx to `m` under LazyMotion, which removes about 17 KB br from the product critical path (about 85 ms of transfer at 1.6 Mbps, plus compile on a slow CPU).
3) Move below-the-fold parts of the 4,829-line Product.tsx (specs, usage guide, content blocks, warranty/quick-buy sheets) into lazy chunks.

Expected: about −1 s perceived first paint on phones and roughly −0.1 to −0.3 s to the real render.
reasons:
The cause is real but over-rated, and fix 1 does not do what the finding says it does.

WHAT IS TRUE (re-measured on the live site, phone profile 360x800 DPR3, CPU x4, 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps, 5 cold runs on /product/esun-pla-plus; output in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Levonis/aa8068a2-6eee-5a26-9836-675f1c2740c2/scratchpad/perf/skeptic-productfallback/live1.json):
- RouteFallback (src/App.tsx:113-139, mounted at App.tsx:905) mounts at a median of 2649 ms and leaves at 3499 ms. For those 850 ms the screen is blank. In the light theme `bg-black` paints the beige page colour, and the header holds only an empty anchor (MotionCharacterAnchor.tsx:57-65). Screencast frames are in shots/A-0.
- FCP is 3564 ms, about fbOff + 60 ms. h1 is at 3845 ms and LCP at 4372 ms.
- vendor-motion is still the last script of the product closure to finish (it ends at about 3250-3400 ms). Note.tsx:21 `import { motion } from 'motion/react'` is still the only edge to it. Live manifest: `_Note-BR8R_Cug.js` imports `_vendor-motion-DDNunUBr.js`. The live Product chunk is now `Product-BRPeh8Sn.js`, but the code is unchanged.

WHAT IS WRONG OR OVERSTATED:
1. It is not a waterfall. The worker writes all 23 closure chunks into the document head as `<link rel=modulepreload>`, right after the `/api/products/<slug>` preload (checked with curl). They download in parallel with the entry. The closure is 23 files, about 91 KB gz or 94 KB br (closure walk of the built manifest), not 130 KB.
2. Fix 1 (ProductDetailSkeleton as the Suspense fallback) does not move FCP. I built the 7c7190b source three ways in scratch: A (as is), F (fix 1) and N (Note.tsx on `m` from motion/react-m under MotionFeatures). Each was served over HTTP/2 with the live document's preload list rewritten to that arm's closure. 7 runs per arm after a warm-up, interleaved (ab1.json):
   - A: FCP 2892, skeleton visible 3166, h1 3528, LCP 4196.
   - F: FCP 3008, skeleton visible 2624, h1 3619, LCP 4208.
   The skeleton is grey spans plus zero-width-space line boxes, and Chrome does not count it as contentful. FCP is still set by the mascot SVG or the arrow icon in Product's own loading header (Product.tsx:2143-2160). Real content does not come earlier either: h1 is +91 ms and LCP +12 ms, which is noise or the small cost of rendering the skeleton on a slow CPU. The only gain is visual: a placeholder replaces the blank screen about 0.54 s earlier in the lab, and at most the 0.85 s live blank window. This only happens on a cold landing on /product/:slug.
